weeks.title: Joint distributions
weeks.summary: Do ya zyada discrete random variables ko ek saath kaise describe karte hain, yeh seekhenge. Joint PMF table se marginal aur conditional probabilities nikalna is week ka main skill hai.
concepts: **Joint PMF**: p(x, y) = P(X = x, Y = y). Yeh batata hai ki X aur Y dono ek saath specific values lein, uski probability kitni hai.
**Valid joint PMF**: har cell p(x, y) ≥ 0 hona chahiye aur saare cells ka total Σ p(x, y) = 1 hona chahiye. Unknown constant nikalne ke liye isi rule ka use hota hai.
**Marginal PMF**: P(X = x) = Σ (over y) p(x, y), yaani table mein X wali row ka sum. Isi tarah Y ka marginal column sum se aata hai.
**Conditional PMF**: P(Y = y | X = x) = p(x, y) / P(X = x). Matlab given X = x wali row ko us row ke total se divide kar do, taaki nayi row ka sum 1 ho jaaye.
**Event probability**: P(X + Y ≤ 2) jaise events ke liye bas un cells ko add karo jo condition satisfy karte hain.
**Teen ya zyada RVs**: p(x, y, z) bhi same tarah kaam karta hai. Kisi ek variable ka marginal chahiye toh baaki variables par sum kar do.

steps: Pehle check karo: 0.1 + 0.2 + 0.1 + 0.2 + 0.3 + 0.1 = 1.0, toh PMF valid hai.

mistakes: P(Y = y | X = x) nikalte waqt galat marginal se divide karna. Jo variable 'given' hai (bar ke right side), usi ke marginal se divide karo.
Table ka total 1 check kiye bina aage badh jaana. Unknown constant wale questions mein yahi pehla step hai.
Yeh maan lena ki p(x, y) = P(X = x) × P(Y = y) hamesha hota hai. Yeh sirf independent RVs ke liye true hai.
revision: Σ over all (x, y) of p(x, y) = 1
P(X = x) = Σ over y of p(x, y) (row sum)
P(Y = y) = Σ over x of p(x, y) (column sum)
P(Y = y | X = x) = p(x, y) / P(X = x)
Kisi event ki probability = condition satisfy karne wale cells ka sum

questions.question: X, Y ∈ {0, 1} ka joint PMF hai: p(0,0) = 0.15, p(0,1) = 0.25, p(1,0) = 0.35, p(1,1) = k. k ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: Saare cells ka sum 1 hona chahiye: 0.15 + 0.25 + 0.35 + k = 1, toh k = 1 − 0.75 = 0.25. Trap: 0.75 known cells ka sum hai, k nahi.

questions.question: Joint PMF: p(1,1) = 0.1, p(1,2) = 0.3, p(2,1) = 0.2, p(2,2) = 0.4. P(Y = 2) kitna hai?
questions.explanation: P(Y = 2) = p(1,2) + p(2,2) = 0.3 + 0.4 = 0.7. Trap: 0.6 = P(X = 2) hai (galat variable ka marginal), aur 0.4 sirf ek cell hai.

questions.question: Same joint PMF: p(1,1) = 0.1, p(1,2) = 0.3, p(2,1) = 0.2, p(2,2) = 0.4. P(X = 2 | Y = 2) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Given Y = 2 hai, toh P(Y = 2) = 0.7 se divide karo: 0.4 / 0.7 = 4/7. Trap: 2/3 = 0.4 / 0.6 hai, jo P(Y = 2 | X = 2) hota hai (galat marginal se divide kiya). 0.4 joint probability hai, conditional nahi.

questions.question: Ek fair coin do baar toss hota hai. X = total heads, Y = 1 agar pehla toss Head ho, warna 0. P(X = 1, Y = 1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Outcomes HH, HT, TH, TT, har ek 1/4. X = 1 aur pehla toss H, dono sirf HT mein hota hai, toh answer 1/4. Trap: 1/2 = P(X = 1) ya P(Y = 1) akele ki probability hai, joint nahi.

questions.question: p(x, y) = c(x + y), jahan x ∈ {1, 2} aur y ∈ {1, 2}. Valid PMF ke liye c kya hona chahiye?
questions.explanation: Chaaron cells: (1,1) → 2c, (1,2) → 3c, (2,1) → 3c, (2,2) → 4c. Total 12c = 1, toh c = 1/12. Trap: 1/9 tab aata hai jab (1,2) aur (2,1) ko ek hi cell gin lo; 1/4 tab jab har cell ko equal maan lo.

questions.question: p(x, y) = (x + y)/12, x ∈ {1, 2}, y ∈ {1, 2}. P(X = 2 | Y = 1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: P(Y = 1) = p(1,1) + p(2,1) = 2/12 + 3/12 = 5/12. Phir P(X = 2 | Y = 1) = (3/12) / (5/12) = 3/5. Trap: 3/7 = p(2,1) / P(X = 2) hai, yaani galat marginal (X ka) se divide kiya. 3/12 sirf joint probability hai.

questions.question: X aur Y ka joint PMF neeche table mein diya hai. P(X + Y = 2) kya hai?
questions.explanation: X + Y = 2 wale cells sirf (1,1) aur (2,0) hain: 0.15 + 0.20 = 0.35. Trap: 0.45 = P(X + Y ≤ 2) hai (= ki jagah ≤ le liya, toh (1,0) bhi jud gaya); 0.25 = P(X = 2) ek marginal hai, yeh event nahi.

questions.question: X, Y ∈ {0, 1} ke chaar cells p(0,0), p(0,1), p(1,0), p(1,1) ki values har option mein isi order mein di hain. Kaunsi list ek valid joint PMF hai?
questions.explanation: Valid joint PMF ke liye har cell ≥ 0 aur total = 1 hona chahiye. 0.25 + 0.35 + 0.15 + 0.25 = 1 aur sab non-negative hain, toh yeh valid hai. Trap: 0.5, −0.1, 0.3, 0.3 ka total 1 hai par ek cell negative hai; pehli list ka total 1.1 aur aakhri ka 0.9 hai.

questions.question: X, Y, Z ∈ {0, 1} ka joint PMF table mein hai. P(Z = 1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Z ka marginal chahiye, toh X aur Y dono par sum karo: z = 1 wale chaar cells 0.10 + 0.10 + 0.05 + 0.20 = 0.45. Trap: 0.55 = P(Z = 0) hai; 0.30 = P(Y = 1, Z = 1) hai, jahan sirf X par sum kiya, Y par nahi.

questions.question: Table se, X = 2 diye hone par Y ka conditional PMF, yaani P(Y = 0 | X = 2), P(Y = 1 | X = 2), P(Y = 2 | X = 2) kya hai?
questions.explanation: P(X = 2) = 0.12 + 0.30 + 0.18 = 0.6. Row ko 0.6 se divide karo: 0.12/0.6 = 0.2, 0.30/0.6 = 0.5, 0.18/0.6 = 0.3 (sum 1). Trap: 0.12, 0.30, 0.18 joint values hain (divide nahi kiya, sum sirf 0.6); 0.22, 0.50, 0.28 Y ka marginal hai (column sums); 0.3, 0.75, 0.45 mein galat row ke total 0.4 se divide kiya, sum 1.5 aata hai.

questions.question: p(x, y) = c × x × y, jahan x ∈ {1, 2, 3} aur y ∈ {1, 2}. P(X ≥ Y) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Total: c × (1 + 2 + 3)(1 + 2) = 18c = 1, toh c = 1/18. X ≥ Y sirf cell (1,2) par fail hota hai, jiski probability 2/18 = 1/9. Toh P(X ≥ Y) = 1 − 1/9 = 8/9. Trap: 11/18 = P(X > Y) hai (barabar wale cells (1,1) aur (2,2) chhoot gaye); 5/6 tab aata hai jab 6 cells ko equally likely maan lo.

questions.question: X, Y ∈ {0, 1}: p(0,0) = 0.2, p(0,1) = a, p(1,0) = b, p(1,1) = 0.3. Diya hai ki P(Y = 1 | X = 0) = 0.6. b kya hai?
questions.explanation: P(X = 0) = 0.2 + a, toh a/(0.2 + a) = 0.6 ⇒ a = 0.12 + 0.6a ⇒ 0.4a = 0.12 ⇒ a = 0.3. Total 1 se b = 1 − 0.2 − 0.3 − 0.3 = 0.2. Trap: 0.38 tab aata hai jab a = 0.6 × 0.2 = 0.12 le lo (row total mein a khud bhi hai, sirf 0.2 nahi); 0.3 a ki value hai, b ki nahi; 0.5 mein a ko ghatana bhool gaye.

questions.question: Ek box mein 2 red aur 3 blue balls hain. Bina replacement 2 balls nikaali. X = 1 agar pehli ball red ho (warna 0), Y = 1 agar doosri ball red ho (warna 0). P(X = 1 | Y = 1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Joint: p(1,1) = (2/5)(1/4) = 1/10 aur p(0,1) = (3/5)(2/4) = 3/10. Toh P(Y = 1) = 1/10 + 3/10 = 2/5. P(X = 1 | Y = 1) = (1/10)/(2/5) = 1/4. Trap: 2/5 = P(X = 1) hai, jaise X aur Y independent hon (bina replacement mein nahi hain); 1/10 joint probability hai; 1/2 = P(Y = 1 | X = 0) hai, galat conditional.

questions.question: p(x, y, z) = c(x + y + z), jahan x, y, z ∈ {0, 1}. P(X = 1 | Z = 1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: 8 cells ka total: har variable 4 cells mein 1 hai, toh Σ(x + y + z) = 12 aur c = 1/12. Z = 1 wale cells: (0,0,1) → 1, (0,1,1) → 2, (1,0,1) → 2, (1,1,1) → 3, total 8/12. Inme X = 1 wale: 2 + 3 = 5, yaani 5/12. P(X = 1 | Z = 1) = (5/12)/(8/12) = 5/8. Trap: 5/12 joint probability hai; 3/8 = P(X = 0 | Z = 1) hai; 2/3 = P(Z = 1) hai.

questions.question: Table mein X aur Y ka joint PMF hai. P(X > Y | X + Y ≥ 2) kya hai?
questions.explanation: X + Y ≥ 2 wale cells: (0,2), (1,1), (1,2), (2,0), (2,1), (2,2), total 0.15 + 0.20 + 0.10 + 0.15 + 0.05 + 0.10 = 0.75. Inme X > Y: (2,0) aur (2,1) = 0.20. Answer 0.20/0.75 = 4/15. Trap: 0.2 joint hai (divide nahi kiya); 2/5 = 0.30/0.75 mein (1,0) bhi gin liya, jo condition X + Y ≥ 2 mein nahi aata; 1/3 = 2/6 sirf cells gin kar aata hai.

weeks.title: Independence and functions
weeks.summary: Kab do RVs independent hote hain, aur X + Y, max(X, Y) jaise functions ka PMF kaise nikalte hain. Binomial aur Poisson ke sums ka shortcut bhi seekhenge.
concepts: **Independence**: X aur Y independent hain agar har (x, y) ke liye p(x, y) = P(X = x) × P(Y = y). Ek bhi cell fail ho jaaye toh dependent.
**Function of RVs**: Z = g(X, Y) ka PMF nikalne ke liye har cell ka Z value likho, phir same Z value wale cells ki probabilities add karo.
**Sum of independent RVs (convolution)**: P(X + Y = z) = Σ over k of P(X = k) × P(Y = z − k). Independence ki wajah se product use kar sakte hain.
**Poisson sum**: X ~ Poisson(λ₁), Y ~ Poisson(λ₂) independent hon toh X + Y ~ Poisson(λ₁ + λ₂).
**Binomial sum**: X ~ Bin(n, p), Y ~ Bin(m, p) independent aur same p ho toh X + Y ~ Bin(n + m, p).
**Max aur min**: independent X, Y ke liye P(max ≤ t) = P(X ≤ t) × P(Y ≤ t) aur P(min > t) = P(X > t) × P(Y > t).
**iid**: independent and identically distributed, yaani sab RVs independent hain aur sab ka distribution same hai.

example.problem: X aur Y independent hain, dono {1, 2, 3} par uniform (har value 1/3). Z = X + Y ka PMF aur P(max(X, Y) ≤ 2) nikalo.
steps: Independent hai, toh har pair (x, y) ki probability = (1/3)(1/3) = 1/9. Total 9 pairs.

mistakes: Sirf ek cell check karke independence declare kar dena. Independent bolne ke liye har cell check karna padta hai; dependent bolne ke liye ek failing cell kaafi hai.
P(max = 1) ko P(X = 1) + P(Y = 1) likh dena. Sahi tareeka complement hai: 1 − P(dono 0).
Binomial sum shortcut ko alag p wale binomials par laga dena. Shortcut tabhi chalta hai jab p same ho.
revision: Independent ⇔ p(x, y) = P(X = x)P(Y = y) har (x, y) ke liye
P(X + Y = z) = Σ P(X = k)P(Y = z − k)
Bin(n, p) + Bin(m, p) = Bin(n + m, p)
P(max ≤ t) = P(X ≤ t)P(Y ≤ t) for independent X, Y

questions.question: X aur Y independent hain. P(X = 1) = 0.4 aur P(Y = 0) = 0.5. P(X = 1, Y = 0) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Independent RVs ke liye joint = product: 0.4 × 0.5 = 0.2. Trap: 0.9 add karne se aata hai, jo 'ya' (OR) type event ke liye bhi galat hoga.

questions.question: X ~ Poisson(2) aur Y ~ Poisson(3) independent hain. X + Y ka distribution kya hai?
questions.explanation: Independent Poisson RVs ke sum mein rates add hote hain: 2 + 3 = 5, toh Poisson(5). Trap: Poisson(6) rates ko multiply karne se aata hai, aur 2.5 average lene se.

questions.question: Joint PMF: p(0,0) = 0.2, p(0,1) = 0.2, p(1,0) = 0.3, p(1,1) = 0.3. X aur Y ke baare mein kya sahi hai?
options: Dependent hain, kyunki table symmetric nahi hai
E[XY] jaane bina kuch nahi keh sakte
Independent hain, kyunki har cell mein p(x, y) = P(X = x)P(Y = y)
questions.explanation: P(X = 0) = 0.4, P(X = 1) = 0.6, P(Y = 0) = P(Y = 1) = 0.5. Check: 0.4 × 0.5 = 0.2 aur 0.6 × 0.5 = 0.3, chaaron cells match. Isliye independent. Trap: alag cells ki values alag hona dependence ka sign nahi hai.

questions.question: X, Y independent hain, dono {1, 2, 3} par uniform. P(X + Y = 5) kya hai?
questions.explanation: X + Y = 5 ke pairs: (2,3) aur (3,2). Har pair 1/9, toh total 2/9. Trap: 1/9 tab aata hai jab (2,3) aur (3,2) ko ek hi gin lo; order matter karta hai.

questions.question: X aur Y iid Bernoulli(0.3) hain. Z = max(X, Y). P(Z = 1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Z = 0 sirf tab jab dono 0 hon: 0.7 × 0.7 = 0.49. Toh P(Z = 1) = 1 − 0.49 = 0.51. Trap: 0.6 = 0.3 + 0.3 hai, jo dono ke 1 hone wale case ko double count karta hai. 0.09 sirf 'dono 1' hai.

questions.question: X ~ Bin(3, 1/2) aur Y ~ Bin(2, 1/2) independent hain. P(X + Y = 1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Same p hai, toh X + Y ~ Bin(5, 1/2). P(X + Y = 1) = 5C1 × (1/2)⁵ = 5/32. Direct check: P(X=1)P(Y=0) + P(X=0)P(Y=1) = (3/8)(1/4) + (1/8)(1/2) = 3/32 + 2/32 = 5/32. Trap: 1/6 tab aata hai jab 0 se 5 tak saari values equally likely maan lo.

questions.question: X aur Y independent hain. P(X = 2) = 0.5 aur P(Y = 3) = 0.2. P(X = 2 | Y = 3) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Independent RVs mein Y ki information X ka distribution nahi badalti: P(X = 2 | Y = 3) = P(X = 2, Y = 3)/P(Y = 3) = (0.5 × 0.2)/0.2 = 0.5. Trap: 0.1 joint probability hai, conditional nahi; 0.2 given event ki probability hai.

questions.question: X ~ Bin(4, 0.3) aur Y ~ Bin(6, 0.3) independent hain. X + Y ka distribution kya hai?
questions.explanation: p same hai (0.3), toh trials add hote hain: X + Y ~ Bin(4 + 6, 0.3) = Bin(10, 0.3). Trap: Bin(10, 0.6) mein p bhi add kar diya, jabki har trial ki success probability 0.3 hi rehti hai; Bin(24, 0.3) mein n multiply kar diye; Bin(5, 0.3) average hai.

questions.question: X ~ Poisson(1) aur Y ~ Poisson(2) independent hain. P(X + Y = 0) kya hai?
questions.explanation: X + Y ~ Poisson(1 + 2) = Poisson(3), toh P(X + Y = 0) = e^(−3) ≈ 0.050. Direct bhi: P(X = 0)P(Y = 0) = e^(−1) × e^(−2) = e^(−3). Trap: e^(−1) + e^(−2) mein probabilities add kar di, multiply karni thi; e^(−2) rates ko multiply (1 × 2) karne se aata hai; e^(−1.5) rates ka average hai.

questions.question: X aur Y independent hain. X ∈ {0, 1, 2} probabilities 0.2, 0.5, 0.3 ke saath, aur Y ∈ {0, 1} probabilities 0.6, 0.4 ke saath. P(X + Y = 2) kya hai?
questions.explanation: X + Y = 2 do tareeke se hota hai: (X = 2, Y = 0) → 0.3 × 0.6 = 0.18, aur (X = 1, Y = 1) → 0.5 × 0.4 = 0.20. Total 0.38. Trap: 0.18 ya 0.20 sirf ek pair hai; convolution mein saare pairs (k, 2 − k) jodne padte hain. 0.12 = P(X + Y = 3) hai.

questions.question: Do fair dice independently roll kiye; X aur Y unke results hain. P(min(X, Y) = 3) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Independent ke liye P(min ≥ t) = P(X ≥ t)P(Y ≥ t). P(min ≥ 3) = (4/6)² = 16/36 aur P(min ≥ 4) = (3/6)² = 9/36. Toh P(min = 3) = 16/36 − 9/36 = 7/36. Trap: 4/9 = P(min ≥ 3) hai, '= 3' nahi; 1/36 sirf (3,3) hai, jabki (3,5), (6,3) jaise pairs ka min bhi 3 hai; 11/36 = P(min = 1) hai.

questions.question: X, Y ∈ {0, 1} independent hain. p(0,0) = 0.12 aur p(0,1) = 0.28 diye hain. p(1,0) kya hai?
questions.explanation: P(X = 0) = 0.12 + 0.28 = 0.4, toh P(X = 1) = 0.6. Independence se P(Y = 0) = P(Y = 0 | X = 0) = 0.12/0.4 = 0.3. Toh p(1,0) = 0.6 × 0.3 = 0.18 (aur p(1,1) = 0.42). Trap: 0.30 = P(Y = 0) hai, joint nahi; 0.42 = p(1,1) hai; 0.12 copy karna maan leta hai ki dono rows same hain, jabki P(X = 1) ≠ P(X = 0).

questions.question: X uniform hai {1, 2, 3} par aur Y uniform hai {1, 2, 3, 4} par, dono independent. P(max(X, Y) = 3) kya hai?
questions.explanation: P(max ≤ 3) = P(X ≤ 3)P(Y ≤ 3) = 1 × 3/4 = 3/4. P(max ≤ 2) = (2/3)(2/4) = 1/3. Toh P(max = 3) = 3/4 − 1/3 = 5/12. Trap: 7/12 = 1/3 + 1/4 mein P(X = 3) aur P(Y = 3) add kar diye, jo (3,3) ko do baar ginta hai aur 'doosra ≤ 3 ho' wali condition bhool jaata hai; 3/4 = P(max ≤ 3) hai; 1/12 sirf (3,3) hai.

questions.question: X ~ Poisson(2) aur Y ~ Poisson(3) independent hain. P(X = 1 | X + Y = 3) kya hai?
questions.explanation: X + Y ~ Poisson(5), toh P(X + Y = 3) = e^(−5) × 5³/3! = 125e^(−5)/6. Numerator: P(X = 1)P(Y = 2) = 2e^(−2) × 9e^(−3)/2 = 9e^(−5). Ratio = 9 × 6/125 = 54/125. Trap: 2e^(−2) = P(X = 1) hai, condition ignore ho gayi; 36/125 tab aata hai jab rates ulte le lo (X ka rate 3 samjho); 2/5 sirf rates ka ratio hai.

questions.question: X aur Y iid hain, har ek ka PMF: P(X = 0) = 0.5, P(X = 1) = 0.3, P(X = 2) = 0.2. P(X > Y) kya hai?
questions.explanation: P(X = Y) = 0.5² + 0.3² + 0.2² = 0.25 + 0.09 + 0.04 = 0.38. iid hone se symmetry: P(X > Y) = P(X < Y) = (1 − 0.38)/2 = 0.31. Direct check: 0.3 × 0.5 + 0.2 × 0.5 + 0.2 × 0.3 = 0.15 + 0.10 + 0.06 = 0.31. Trap: 0.62 = P(X ≠ Y) hai, 2 se divide nahi kiya; 0.38 = P(X = Y); 1/3 teen cases (>, =, <) ko equally likely maan leta hai.

weeks.title: Expectation, covariance, correlation
weeks.summary: Mean, variance, covariance aur correlation discrete RVs ke liye kaise nikalte hain. Linearity aur Var(X + Y) ka formula is week ke sabse useful tools hain.
concepts: **Expectation**: E[X] = Σ x × P(X = x). Yeh long-run average value hai.
**E[g(X)]**: E[g(X)] = Σ g(x) × P(X = x). g(X) ka PMF alag se banane ki zaroorat nahi.
**Linearity**: E[aX + bY + c] = aE[X] + bE[Y] + c. Yeh hamesha true hai, independence ki zaroorat nahi.
**Variance**: Var(X) = E[X²] − (E[X])², aur Var(aX + b) = a² Var(X). Constant b variance ko change nahi karta.
**Covariance**: Cov(X, Y) = E[XY] − E[X]E[Y]. Positive matlab dono saath badhte hain, negative matlab ek badhe toh doosra ghate.
**Var of sum**: Var(X ± Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y) ± 2Cov(X, Y). Independent ho toh Cov = 0.
**Correlation**: ρ = Cov(X, Y) / (σX σY), hamesha −1 ≤ ρ ≤ 1. Yeh unit-free measure hai linear relation ka.
**Zero covariance ≠ independence**: Independent ⇒ Cov = 0, lekin Cov = 0 se independence prove nahi hoti.

steps: XY sirf (1,1) par 1 hai, toh E[XY] = 0.4.

mistakes: Var(3X) = 3Var(X) likhna. Constant bahar aate waqt square hota hai: Var(3X) = 9Var(X).
Var(X − Y) = Var(X) − Var(Y) likhna. Variances hamesha add hote hain; sirf covariance ka sign badalta hai.
Cov = 0 dekh kar independent bol dena. Y = X² jaise cases mein Cov 0 ho sakta hai par dependence clear hai.
revision: E[aX + bY + c] = aE[X] + bE[Y] + c
Var(X ± Y) = Var X + Var Y ± 2Cov(X, Y)

questions.question: E[X] = 3 aur E[Y] = −1. E[2X − 3Y + 4] kya hai?
questions.explanation: Linearity: 2(3) − 3(−1) + 4 = 6 + 3 + 4 = 13. Trap: 7 tab aata hai jab −3 × −1 ko −3 le lo (sign mistake).

questions.question: Var(X) = 4. Var(3X + 5) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X) = 9 × 4 = 36. Constant 5 sirf shift karta hai, spread nahi. Trap: 12 mein a ko square nahi kiya, aur 41 / 17 mein constant 5 add kar diya.

questions.question: X values −1, 0, 1 leta hai probabilities 0.25, 0.5, 0.25 ke saath. Var(X) kya hai?
questions.explanation: E[X] = −0.25 + 0 + 0.25 = 0. E[X²] = 1(0.25) + 0 + 1(0.25) = 0.5. Var = 0.5 − 0² = 0.5. Trap: mean 0 hone se variance 0 nahi hota; variance spread naapta hai.

questions.question: E[X] = 2, E[Y] = 3 aur E[XY] = 7. Cov(X, Y) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Cov = E[XY] − E[X]E[Y] = 7 − 6 = 1. Trap: 7 sirf E[XY] hai aur 6 sirf E[X]E[Y]; covariance dono ka difference hai.

questions.question: Var(X) = 4, Var(Y) = 9, Cov(X, Y) = −2. Var(X − Y) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Var(X − Y) = Var X + Var Y − 2Cov = 4 + 9 − 2(−2) = 17. Trap: 13 mein covariance ignore hua, 9 mein sign galat laga, aur 5 mein variances subtract kar diye.

questions.question: X uniform hai {−1, 0, 1} par (har value 1/3) aur Y = X². Kaunsa statement sahi hai?
options: Cov(X, Y) = 0, lekin X aur Y independent nahi hain
Cov(X, Y) = 0, isliye X aur Y independent hain
Cov(X, Y) > 0, kyunki Y poori tarah X par depend karta hai
questions.explanation: E[X] = 0 aur E[XY] = E[X³] = (−1 + 0 + 1)/3 = 0, toh Cov = 0. Lekin P(X = 0, Y = 1) = 0 jabki P(X = 0)P(Y = 1) = (1/3)(2/3) ≠ 0, toh dependent. Trap: 2/3 = E[Y] hai; aur Cov = 0 se independence nahi milti.

questions.question: X ∈ {0, 1, 2} probabilities 0.3, 0.4, 0.3 ke saath. E[X²] kya hai?
questions.explanation: E[X²] = 0²(0.3) + 1²(0.4) + 2²(0.3) = 0 + 0.4 + 1.2 = 1.6. Trap: 1 = (E[X])² hai (E[X] = 1), aur E[X²] ≠ (E[X])²; 0.6 variance hai (1.6 − 1); 5/3 squares 0, 1, 4 ka simple average hai, probabilities ignore karke.

questions.question: Var(X) = 4, Var(Y) = 9 aur Cov(X, Y) = −3. Correlation ρ(X, Y) kya hai?
questions.explanation: σX = √4 = 2, σY = √9 = 3. ρ = −3/(2 × 3) = −0.5. Trap: −1/12 = −3/36 mein SDs ki jagah variances multiply kar diye; −0.75 = −3/4 mein sirf ek variance se divide kiya; 0.5 mein negative sign kho gaya.

questions.question: Cov(X, Y) = 3. Cov(2X + 1, −Y + 5) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Cov(aX + b, cY + d) = ac Cov(X, Y). Yahan a = 2, c = −1, toh 2 × (−1) × 3 = −6. Constants 1 aur 5 covariance ko change nahi karte. Trap: 6 mein −1 ka sign bhool gaye; −12 mein 2 ko square kar diya, jaise variance mein hota hai; −3 mein factor 2 chhoot gaya.

questions.question: Var(X) = 9, Var(Y) = 16 aur ρ(X, Y) = 0.5. Var(X + Y) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Cov = ρ σX σY = 0.5 × 3 × 4 = 6. Var(X + Y) = 9 + 16 + 2(6) = 37. Trap: 25 mein covariance ignore kiya (jaise X, Y independent hon); 31 mein 2 ka factor bhool gaye; 13 = 25 − 12 mein covariance ka sign ulta laga diya.

questions.question: X, Y ∈ {0, 1}: p(0,0) = 0.3, p(0,1) = 0.2, p(1,0) = 0.1, p(1,1) = 0.4. Cov(X, Y) kya hai?
questions.explanation: E[X] = P(X = 1) = 0.1 + 0.4 = 0.5. E[Y] = P(Y = 1) = 0.2 + 0.4 = 0.6. E[XY] = p(1,1) = 0.4. Cov = 0.4 − 0.5 × 0.6 = 0.1. Trap: 0.4 sirf E[XY] hai aur 0.3 sirf E[X]E[Y]; −0.1 mein subtraction ulta kar diya.

questions.question: Var(X) = 4, Var(Y) = 1 aur Cov(X, Y) = 1.5. Var(2X − 3Y) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Var(aX + bY) = a²Var X + b²Var Y + 2ab Cov. a = 2, b = −3: 4(4) + 9(1) + 2(2)(−3)(1.5) = 16 + 9 − 18 = 7. Trap: 43 mein cross term ka sign + le liya; 25 mein covariance ignore kiya; 22 = 16 + 9 − 3 mein cross term ko ab = −6 se multiply karna bhool gaye.

questions.question: E[X] = 1, E[Y] = 2, Var(X) = 2, Var(Y) = 3 aur Var(X + Y) = 8. E[XY] kya hai?
questions.explanation: Var(X + Y) = Var X + Var Y + 2Cov ⇒ 8 = 5 + 2Cov ⇒ Cov = 1.5. Phir E[XY] = Cov + E[X]E[Y] = 1.5 + 2 = 3.5. Trap: 1.5 sirf Cov hai; 5 tab aata hai jab 2 se divide bhool kar Cov = 3 le lo; −0.5 mein E[X]E[Y] ko add karne ki jagah subtract kiya.

questions.question: X aur Y ka joint PMF table mein hai. Var(X + Y) kya hai?

5 students apne caps ek dher mein rakhte hain, phir har koi randomly ek cap utha leta hai (har arrangement equally likely). X = jitne students ko apna hi cap mila. E[X] kya hai? (Hint: X = I₁ + ... + I₅ likho, jahan Iᵢ = 1 agar student i ko apna cap mile, warna 0.)
questions.explanation: X = I₁ + ... + I₅, jahan Iᵢ = 1 agar student i ko apna cap mile. P(Iᵢ = 1) = 1/5, toh E[Iᵢ] = 1/5. Linearity (independence ki zaroorat nahi): E[X] = 5 × 1/5 = 1. Trap: 1/5 ek student ki probability hai, total expected count nahi; 1/120 = 1/5! sabko apna cap milne ki probability hai; 5/2 sirf 0 se 5 ka midpoint hai.

weeks.title: Continuous random variables
weeks.summary: Continuous RVs ko PDF aur CDF se describe karna seekhenge. Integration se probability, mean aur variance nikalna is week ka core hai.
concepts: **PDF**: f(x) ≥ 0 aur ∫ f(x) dx = 1 (poori range par). Probability area hai: P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫ from a to b of f(x) dx.
**Single point ki probability zero**: continuous X ke liye P(X = a) = 0, isliye P(X < a) aur P(X ≤ a) same hain.
**CDF**: F(x) = P(X ≤ x). Yeh non-decreasing hai, 0 se 1 tak jaata hai, aur P(a < X ≤ b) = F(b) − F(a).
**PDF aur CDF ka relation**: f(x) = F′(x), yaani CDF ko differentiate karo toh PDF milta hai.
**Density probability nahi hai**: f(x) ki value 1 se zyada ho sakti hai (jaise Uniform(0, 0.5) mein f = 2). Sirf area ≤ 1 hona chahiye.
**Mean aur variance**: E[X] = ∫ x f(x) dx, E[X²] = ∫ x² f(x) dx, Var(X) = E[X²] − (E[X])².

example.problem: f(x) = 2x, 0 ≤ x ≤ 1 (baaki jagah 0). Check karo ki yeh valid PDF hai, phir F(x), P(X ≤ 0.5), E[X] aur Var(X) nikalo.
steps: ∫ from 0 to 1 of 2x dx = [x²] from 0 to 1 = 1, aur f ≥ 0, toh valid PDF.
F(x) = ∫ from 0 to x of 2t dt = x² (0 ≤ x ≤ 1 ke liye).
E[X] = ∫ from 0 to 1 of x × 2x dx = 2/3.
E[X²] = ∫ from 0 to 1 of x² × 2x dx = 2/4 = 1/2.

mistakes: f(a) ko P(X = a) samajh lena. Continuous case mein kisi ek point ki probability 0 hoti hai; f(a) sirf density hai.
Var nikalte waqt E[X²] ki jagah E[X] use kar lena. E[X²] ke liye x² × f(x) integrate karo.
Normalising constant nikalte waqt antiderivative ka divisor bhool jaana, jaise ∫x² dx = x³/3, sirf x³ nahi.
revision: P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫ from a to b of f(x) dx = F(b) − F(a)
E[X] = ∫ x f(x) dx; Var = E[X²] − (E[X])²

questions.question: f(x) = c x², 0 ≤ x ≤ 3 par (baaki 0). c kya hona chahiye?
questions.explanation: ∫ from 0 to 3 of c x² dx = c × 27/3 = 9c = 1, toh c = 1/9. Trap: 1/27 tab aata hai jab antiderivative x³/3 mein /3 bhool jao.

questions.question: X ek continuous random variable hai jiska PDF f aur CDF F hai. P(X = 2) kya hai?
options: f(2), yaani us point par density
questions.explanation: Continuous RV ke liye kisi bhi single point ki probability 0 hoti hai, kyunki ek point ke upar area zero hai. Trap: f(2) density hai, probability nahi; F(2) = P(X ≤ 2) hai.

questions.question: X ka CDF hai F(x) = x², 0 ≤ x ≤ 1 (x < 0 par 0, x > 1 par 1). P(0.5 < X ≤ 1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: P(0.5 < X ≤ 1) = F(1) − F(0.5) = 1 − 0.25 = 0.75. Trap: 0.25 sirf F(0.5) hai, aur 0.5 tab aata hai jab CDF ko linear maan lo.

questions.question: f(x) = 3x², 0 ≤ x ≤ 1. E[X] kya hai?
questions.explanation: E[X] = ∫ from 0 to 1 of x × 3x² dx = 3 × (1/4) = 3/4. Trap: 3/5 = ∫ x² × 3x² dx = E[X²] hai, E[X] nahi. 1/2 interval ka midpoint hai, jo sirf uniform ke liye mean hota hai.

questions.question: X ka CDF hai F(x) = 1 − 1/x², x ≥ 1 ke liye (x < 1 par 0). X ka PDF kya hai (x ≥ 1 par)?
questions.explanation: f(x) = F′(x) = d/dx (1 − x⁻²) = 2x⁻³ = 2/x³. Trap: −2/x³ sign galat hai (PDF negative nahi ho sakta), aur x − 1/x integrate kar diya, differentiate nahi.

questions.question: f(x) = 3x², 0 ≤ x ≤ 1. Var(X) kya hai?
questions.explanation: E[X] = 3/4, E[X²] = ∫ 3x⁴ dx = 3/5. Var = 3/5 − 9/16 = (48 − 45)/80 = 3/80. Trap: 3/16 = 3/4 − 9/16 hai, jahan E[X²] ki jagah E[X] le liya. 3/5 sirf E[X²] hai.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa function interval [0, 2] par valid PDF hai (baaki jagah f = 0)?
questions.explanation: Valid PDF ke liye f ≥ 0 aur area 1 chahiye. ∫ from 0 to 2 of x/2 dx = 4/4 = 1, aur x/2 ≥ 0. Trap: f(x) = x aur f(x) = 1 dono ka area 2 hai; x − 1 ka area 0 hai aur yeh [0, 1) par negative bhi hai.

questions.question: f(x) = 4x³, 0 ≤ x ≤ 1 (baaki 0). P(X ≤ 1/2) kya hai?
questions.explanation: F(x) = ∫ from 0 to x of 4t³ dt = x⁴. P(X ≤ 1/2) = (1/2)⁴ = 1/16. Trap: 15/16 = P(X > 1/2) hai; 1/2 = f(1/2) hai, jo density hai, probability nahi; 1/8 = (1/2)³ mein antiderivative ki power galat li.

questions.question: f(x) = 3, 0 ≤ x ≤ 1/3 (baaki jagah 0). Kya yeh valid PDF hai?
options: Nahi, kyunki f(x) = 3 > 1 aur probability 1 se zyada nahi ho sakti
Haan, kyunki f(x) ≥ 0 aur total area 3 × 1/3 = 1 hai
Haan, kyunki har constant function valid PDF hota hai
questions.explanation: Density 1 se badi ho sakti hai; condition sirf f ≥ 0 aur total area = 1 hai. Yahan area = 3 × 1/3 = 1, toh valid. Trap: f(x) probability nahi hai, isliye f = 3 allowed hai; area 3 tab hota jab interval ki length 1 hoti; har constant valid nahi hota, constant × length = 1 hona chahiye.

questions.question: f(x) = x/8, 0 ≤ x ≤ 4. X ka median m (jahan F(m) = 1/2) kya hai?
questions.explanation: F(x) = ∫ from 0 to x of t/8 dt = x²/16. m²/16 = 1/2 ⇒ m² = 8 ⇒ m = 2√2 ≈ 2.83. Trap: 2 interval ka midpoint hai, jo sirf symmetric density ka median hota; 8/3 mean hai, median nahi; 4 tab aata hai jab density f(m) = m/8 = 1/2 solve karo, jabki CDF = 1/2 chahiye.

questions.question: f(x) = 2x, 0 ≤ x ≤ 1. E[1/X] kya hai?
questions.explanation: E[g(X)] = ∫ g(x) f(x) dx = ∫ from 0 to 1 of (1/x)(2x) dx = ∫ from 0 to 1 of 2 dx = 2. Trap: 3/2 = 1/E[X] = 1/(2/3) hai, aur E[1/X] ≠ 1/E[X]; 2/3 = E[X] hai, g lagana bhool gaye.

questions.question: f(x) = cx jab 0 ≤ x ≤ 1, aur f(x) = c(2 − x) jab 1 < x ≤ 2 (baaki 0). P(0.5 ≤ X ≤ 1.5) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Graph ek triangle hai, area (1/2) × 2 × c = c = 1, toh c = 1. Tails: P(X < 0.5) = ∫ from 0 to 0.5 of x dx = 1/8, aur symmetry se P(X > 1.5) = 1/8. Toh P(0.5 ≤ X ≤ 1.5) = 1 − 2/8 = 3/4. Trap: 1/2 tab aata hai jab density ko uniform maan kar length ratio lo; 7/8 mein sirf ek tail ghatayi; 1/4 dono tails ka total hai.

questions.question: f(x) = k(1 − x²), −1 ≤ x ≤ 1 (baaki 0). Var(X) kya hai?
questions.explanation: ∫ from −1 to 1 of (1 − x²) dx = 2 − 2/3 = 4/3, toh k = 3/4. Density 0 ke around symmetric hai, toh E[X] = 0. E[X²] = (3/4) ∫ from −1 to 1 of (x² − x⁴) dx = (3/4)(2/3 − 2/5) = (3/4)(4/15) = 1/5. Var = 1/5 − 0² = 1/5. Trap: 4/15 mein k = 3/4 multiply karna bhool gaye; 1/3 Uniform(−1, 1) ka variance hai; 3/4 sirf k hai.

questions.question: f(x) = a + bx, 0 ≤ x ≤ 1, ek valid PDF hai aur E[X] = 7/12. a aur b kya hain?
questions.explanation: Area: a + b/2 = 1. Mean: ∫ x(a + bx) dx = a/2 + b/3 = 7/12. Pehli equation se a = 1 − b/2; daalo: 1/2 − b/4 + b/3 = 1/2 + b/12 = 7/12 ⇒ b = 1, a = 1/2. Trap: baaki teeno options bhi area 1 dete hain (valid PDFs hain), par unke mean 1/2, 2/3 aur 5/8 hain; sirf area check karke ruk jaana kaafi nahi.

questions.question: f(x) = (3/8)x², 0 ≤ x ≤ 2 (baaki 0). P(X > 1 | X > 0.5) kya hai?
questions.explanation: F(x) = x³/8. P(X > 1) = 1 − 1/8 = 7/8 aur P(X > 0.5) = 1 − (0.5)³/8 = 1 − 1/64 = 63/64. {X > 1} event {X > 0.5} ke andar hai, toh conditional = (7/8)/(63/64) = 56/63 = 8/9. Trap: 7/8 mein condition ignore ki; 2/3 = (2 − 1)/(2 − 0.5) length ratio hai, jo sirf uniform ke liye sahi hota; 63/64 given event ki probability hai.

weeks.title: Common continuous distributions
weeks.summary: Uniform, Exponential aur Normal distributions ke formulas, properties aur standard calculations. Normal ko standardize karke Φ table use karna practice karenge.
concepts: **Uniform(a, b)**: f(x) = 1/(b − a) on [a, b]. Mean = (a + b)/2, Var = (b − a)²/12. Probability = length ratio.
**Exponential(λ)**: f(x) = λe^(−λx), x ≥ 0. P(X > t) = e^(−λt), Mean = 1/λ, Var = 1/λ². Waiting time model karne ke liye use hota hai.
**Memoryless property**: Exponential ke liye P(X > s + t | X > s) = P(X > t). Jitna wait ho chuka, usse aage ka wait affect nahi hota.
**Normal(μ, σ²)**: bell-shaped, μ ke around symmetric. Dhyan do: second parameter variance σ² hai, standard deviation σ nahi.
**Standardization**: Z = (X − μ)/σ ~ N(0, 1). Phir P(X ≤ x) = Φ((x − μ)/σ), aur Φ(−z) = 1 − Φ(z).
**68-95-99.7 rule**: Normal mein lagbhag 68%, 95%, 99.7% data μ ± 1σ, 2σ, 3σ ke andar hota hai. Useful Φ values: Φ(1) ≈ 0.8413, Φ(1.96) ≈ 0.975, Φ(2) ≈ 0.9772.

example.problem: Ek bulb ki lifetime Exponential hai jiska mean 500 hours hai. (a) P(lifetime > 1000 hours)? (b) Agar bulb 300 hours chal chuka hai, toh aur 1000 hours chalne ki probability?
steps: Toh (b) ka answer bhi e^(−2) ≈ 0.135 hai, pichle 300 hours ka koi asar nahi.

mistakes: N(50, 100) mein 100 ko σ maan lena. Yeh variance hai, toh σ = 10.
Exponential mein λ aur mean confuse karna. Mean 1/λ hai; 'mean 4' ka matlab λ = 1/4.
Upper tail chahiye tha aur Φ(z) hi likh diya. P(X > x) = 1 − Φ(z).
revision: Uniform(a, b): mean (a + b)/2, var (b − a)²/12
Exponential(λ): P(X > t) = e^(−λt), mean 1/λ, var 1/λ²
Memoryless: P(X > s + t | X > s) = P(X > t)

questions.question: X ~ Uniform(2, 10). Mean aur variance kya hain?
questions.explanation: Mean = (2 + 10)/2 = 6. Var = (10 − 2)²/12 = 64/12 = 16/3. Trap: 2/3 = 8/12 mein (b − a) ko square nahi kiya; 64 mein /12 bhool gaye; 4 = (b − a)/2 hai, mean nahi.

questions.question: X ~ Exponential(λ = 0.5). E[X] kya hai?
questions.explanation: Exponential ka mean 1/λ = 1/0.5 = 2. Trap: 0.5 rate hai, mean nahi; 4 = 1/λ² variance hai.

questions.question: X ~ Uniform(0, 10). P(3 < X < 7) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Uniform mein probability = length / total length = (7 − 3)/10 = 0.4. Trap: 0.7 = P(X < 7) hai aur 0.3 = P(X < 3); dono ka difference chahiye.

questions.question: X ~ N(50, 100) (yahan 100 variance hai). P(X > 70) kya hai? (Φ(2) ≈ 0.9772 use karo)
Bus ka waiting time Exponential hai, mean 4 minutes. Tum 3 minutes se wait kar rahe ho. Aur 4 minutes se zyada wait karne ki probability?
questions.explanation: λ = 1/4. Memoryless se P(X > 3 + 4 | X > 3) = P(X > 4) = e^(−4/4) = e^(−1) ≈ 0.368. Trap: e^(−7/4) = P(X > 7) hai, jo past wait ko condition nahi karta. 1 − e^(−1) = P(X ≤ 4) hai.

questions.question: Exam scores ~ N(60, 15²). Top 2.5% students ka cutoff score kya hai? (Φ(1.645) ≈ 0.95, Φ(1.96) ≈ 0.975)
questions.explanation: Top 2.5% ka matlab P(X > c) = 0.025, yaani Φ(z) = 0.975, z = 1.96. c = 60 + 1.96 × 15 = 60 + 29.4 = 89.4. Trap: 84.7 mein 1.645 use hua (wo top 5% hai); 501 mein σ ki jagah variance 225 multiply kiya; 75 sirf μ + σ hai.

questions.question: Ek call centre mein agli call ka waiting time Exponential hai, mean 5 minutes. P(waiting time > 10 minutes) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Mean 5 ⇒ λ = 1/5. P(X > 10) = e^(−λ × 10) = e^(−10/5) = e^(−2) ≈ 0.135. Trap: e^(−50) mein λ = 5 le liya (mean ko rate samjha); 1 − e^(−2) = P(X ≤ 10) hai; e^(−1/2) mein mean/t ulta le liya.

questions.question: X ~ N(70, 16). P(X < 74) kya hai? (Φ(1) ≈ 0.8413, Φ(0.25) ≈ 0.5987)
questions.explanation: σ = √16 = 4. z = (74 − 70)/4 = 1. P(X < 74) = Φ(1) ≈ 0.8413. Trap: 0.5987 tab aata hai jab 16 ko σ maan lo (z = 4/16 = 0.25); 0.1587 upper tail hai; 0.6826 μ − σ aur μ + σ ke beech ki probability hai.

questions.question: Z ~ N(0, 1) aur Φ(1.5) ≈ 0.9332. P(Z < −1.5) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Symmetry: Φ(−z) = 1 − Φ(z), toh P(Z < −1.5) = 1 − 0.9332 = 0.0668. Trap: 0.9332 = P(Z < 1.5) hai (minus sign ignore kiya); 0.1336 dono tails ka total hai; 0.4332 = Φ(1.5) − 0.5 hai.

questions.question: X ~ Uniform(0, 20). P(X > 15 | X > 5) kya hai?
questions.explanation: P(X > 15) = 5/20 aur P(X > 5) = 15/20. Conditional = (5/20)/(15/20) = 1/3. Trap: 1/2 tab aata hai jab memoryless property laga do (P(X > 10) = 1/2); woh sirf Exponential ke liye hai, Uniform ke liye nahi. 1/4 mein condition ignore ki; 3/4 = P(X > 5) hai.

questions.question: Ek exam ke marks ~ N(65, 25). Lagbhag kitne percent students ke marks 55 aur 75 ke beech honge?
questions.explanation: σ = √25 = 5. 55 aur 75 = 65 ∓ 10 = μ ∓ 2σ. 68-95-99.7 rule se lagbhag 95%. Trap: 68% tab aata hai jab 10 ki doori ko 1σ samjho (σ = 10 maan liya); 47.5% sirf ek side (65 se 75) hai; 99.7% ±3σ ke liye hai.

questions.question: Phone calls ki duration Exponential hai, mean 3 minutes. Kis time t ke liye P(duration > t) = 0.25 hoga?
questions.explanation: λ = 1/3. e^(−t/3) = 1/4 ⇒ t/3 = ln 4 ⇒ t = 3 ln 4 ≈ 4.16 minutes. Trap: (ln 4)/3 mein λ = 3 le liya; 3 ln(4/3) tab aata hai jab P(X ≤ t) = 0.25 solve kar do (yeh lower quartile hai); 2.25 = 0.75 × 3 ek linear guess hai, exponential curve linear nahi hota.

questions.question: Ek test ke scores ~ N(100, 15²). Ek random student ka score 85 aur 130 ke beech hone ki probability kya hai? (Φ(1) ≈ 0.8413, Φ(2) ≈ 0.9772)
X ~ N(50, σ²) aur P(X > 60) = 0.0228. σ kya hai? (Φ(2) ≈ 0.9772)
questions.explanation: P(X > 60) = 0.0228 ⇒ Φ((60 − 50)/σ) = 0.9772 ⇒ (60 − 50)/σ = 2 ⇒ σ = 10/2 = 5. Trap: 25 = σ² hai, σ nahi; 10 tab aata hai jab z = 1 le lo; 20 = 10 × 2 mein divide ki jagah multiply kiya.

questions.question: X ~ Uniform(a, b) ka mean 6 aur variance 3 hai. b kya hai?
questions.explanation: (a + b)/2 = 6 ⇒ a + b = 12. (b − a)²/12 = 3 ⇒ (b − a)² = 36 ⇒ b − a = 6. Toh b = 9 aur a = 3. Check: Uniform(3, 9) ka mean 6, variance 36/12 = 3. Trap: 24 mein (b − a)/12 = 3 likha (square bhool gaye); 7.5 mein variance 3 ko hi length b − a samjha; 6 + 3√3 mein 3 ko SD maan kar (b − a)²/12 = 9 solve kiya.

weeks.title: Functions of continuous RVs
weeks.summary: Agar X ka distribution pata hai toh Y = g(X) ka distribution kaise nikalein. CDF method aur monotone transformation formula dono seekhenge.
concepts: **CDF method**: FY(y) = P(Y ≤ y) = P(g(X) ≤ y). Is event ko X ke terms mein likho, X ka CDF use karo, phir differentiate karke Y ka PDF lo.
**Monotone transformation formula**: agar g strictly increasing ya decreasing hai aur x = h(y) inverse hai, toh fY(y) = fX(h(y)) × |h′(y)|.
**Linear transform**: Y = aX + b ke liye fY(y) = (1/|a|) fX((y − b)/a). Range bhi shift aur scale hoti hai.
**Normal linear rahta hai**: X ~ N(μ, σ²) ⇒ aX + b ~ N(aμ + b, a²σ²).
**Uniform aur Exponential scaling**: X ~ Uniform(0, 1) ⇒ aX + b ~ Uniform(b, a + b) (a > 0). X ~ Exp(λ) ⇒ cX ~ Exp(λ/c) (c > 0).
**Non-monotone g (jaise X²)**: Y ≤ y ka matlab −√y ≤ X ≤ √y. Dono sides ka area count karna padta hai.
**Shortcut for mean**: sirf E[g(X)] chahiye toh ∫ g(x) fX(x) dx kaafi hai, Y ka PDF nikalne ki zaroorat nahi.

example.problem: X ~ Uniform(0, 1) aur Y = −ln(X). Y ka distribution nikalo.
steps: X (0, 1) mein hai, toh −ln X (0, ∞) mein hai. Toh y ≥ 0 lo.
FY(y) = P(−ln X ≤ y) = P(ln X ≥ −y) = P(X ≥ e^(−y)).
X uniform hai, toh P(X ≥ e^(−y)) = 1 − e^(−y).
Answer: Y ~ Exponential(1). Isi trick se computer uniform random numbers se exponential numbers banata hai.

mistakes: Monotone formula mein |h′(y)| factor bhool jaana. Uske bina density ka area 1 nahi aayega.
Y = X² mein sirf positive root lena jab X negative values bhi le sakta hai. −√y wali side bhi count karo.
aX + b ka variance a²σ² + b likh dena. Constant b variance mein nahi aata.
revision: FY(y) = P(g(X) ≤ y), phir fY = FY′
aX + b ~ N(aμ + b, a²σ²) jab X normal ho

questions.question: X ~ N(2, 9). Y = 3X − 1 ka distribution kya hai?
questions.explanation: Mean = 3(2) − 1 = 5, Var = 3² × 9 = 81. Toh N(5, 81). Trap: 27 mein 3 ko square nahi kiya; N(6, 81) mein −1 bhool gaye.

questions.question: X ~ Uniform(0, 2) aur Y = 3X + 1. Y ka distribution kya hai?
questions.explanation: X = 0 par Y = 1, X = 2 par Y = 7. Linear transform uniform ko uniform hi rakhta hai, toh Y ~ Uniform(1, 7). Trap: Uniform(0, 6) mein +1 shift bhool gaye.

questions.question: X ~ Uniform(0, 1) aur Y = X². 0 ≤ y ≤ 1 ke liye Y ka CDF FY(y) kya hai?
questions.explanation: FY(y) = P(X² ≤ y) = P(X ≤ √y) = √y (kyunki X ≥ 0 aur uniform). Trap: y² tab aata hai jab transformation ko ulta laga do.

questions.question: X ~ Uniform(0, 1) aur Y = X². 0 < y < 1 par Y ka PDF kya hai?
questions.explanation: FY(y) = √y, toh fY(y) = d/dy (√y) = 1/(2√y). Check: ∫ from 0 to 1 of 1/(2√y) dy = 1. Trap: 1/√y ka area 2 aata hai, valid PDF nahi; √y CDF hai, PDF nahi.

questions.question: X ~ Exponential(λ = 2) aur Y = 3X. Y ka distribution kya hai?
questions.explanation: P(Y > y) = P(X > y/3) = e^(−2y/3), toh Y ~ Exponential(2/3). Intuition: time 3 guna lamba hua, toh rate 3 guna kam hua. Trap: Exponential(6) mein rate ko multiply kar diya; 3/2 Y ka mean hai, rate nahi.

questions.question: X ~ Uniform(−1, 2) aur Y = X². P(Y ≤ 1/4) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Y ≤ 1/4 ⇔ −1/2 ≤ X ≤ 1/2. Length 1, total length 3, toh probability 1/3. Trap: 1/6 tab aata hai jab sirf positive side 0 se 1/2 lo; negative X bhi square hokar chhota hota hai.

questions.question: X ~ Uniform(0, 2) aur Y = X². E[Y] kya hai?
questions.explanation: Shortcut: E[Y] = E[X²] = ∫ from 0 to 2 of x² × (1/2) dx = (1/2)(8/3) = 4/3. Y ka PDF nikalne ki zaroorat nahi. Trap: 1 = (E[X])² hai, aur E[g(X)] ≠ g(E[X]); 1/3 X ka variance hai; 2 = (0² + 2²)/2 endpoints ka average hai.

questions.question: X ka PDF fX hai aur Y = 2X + 3. Y ka PDF fY(y) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Inverse x = h(y) = (y − 3)/2 aur |h′(y)| = 1/2. Formula fY(y) = fX(h(y)) |h′(y)| = (1/2) fX((y − 3)/2). Trap: factor 2 tab aata hai jab g′ = 2 se multiply karo, h′ = 1/2 se nahi (tab total area 4 ho jaayega); fX(2y + 3) mein inverse ki jagah g hi laga diya; (y + 3)/2 mein inverse ka sign galat hai.

questions.question: X ~ Uniform(1, 3) aur Y = X². P(Y ≤ 4) kya hai?
questions.explanation: X > 0 hai, toh Y ≤ 4 ⇔ X ≤ 2. P(X ≤ 2) = (2 − 1)/(3 − 1) = 1/2. Trap: 3/8 = (4 − 1)/(9 − 1) tab aata hai jab Y ko Uniform(1, 9) maan lo, jabki X² uniform nahi rehta; 4/9 mein Y ko Uniform(0, 9) jaisa treat kiya.

questions.question: X ~ Exponential(1) aur Y = √X. y > 0 par Y ka PDF fY(y) kya hai?
questions.explanation: CDF method: FY(y) = P(√X ≤ y) = P(X ≤ y²) = 1 − e^(−y²). Differentiate: fY(y) = 2y e^(−y²). Trap: 1 − e^(−y²) CDF hai, PDF nahi; e^(−y²) mein chain rule ka 2y bhool gaye; e^(−√y)/(2√y) Y = X² ka PDF hai (transformation ulti laga di).

questions.question: X ~ Uniform(0, 1) aur Y = e^X. E[Y] kya hai?
questions.explanation: E[e^X] = ∫ from 0 to 1 of e^x × 1 dx = e − 1 ≈ 1.718. Trap: e^(1/2) = g(E[X]) hai; non-linear g ke liye E[g(X)] ≠ g(E[X]). (e + 1)/2 endpoints e⁰ aur e¹ ka average hai, jo sirf linear g ke liye sahi hota; e sabse badi value hai, mean nahi.

questions.question: X ~ Uniform(0, 1) aur Y = 1/X. Y ka PDF (support ke saath) kya hai?
questions.explanation: X ∈ (0, 1) ⇒ Y = 1/X ∈ (1, ∞). Inverse x = 1/y, h′(y) = −1/y², |h′(y)| = 1/y². fY(y) = 1 × 1/y² = 1/y², y > 1. Check: ∫ from 1 to ∞ of 1/y² dy = 1. Trap: −1/y² mein absolute value bhool gaye (density negative nahi ho sakti); 1/y ka area infinite hai; 0 < y < 1 galat support hai, kyunki 1/X hamesha 1 se bada hai.

questions.question: X ~ Uniform(−2, 2) aur Y = X². 0 < y < 4 par Y ka PDF kya hai?
questions.explanation: FY(y) = P(−√y ≤ X ≤ √y) = 2√y/4 = √y/2. Differentiate: fY(y) = 1/(4√y). Check: ∫ from 0 to 4 of 1/(4√y) dy = (1/4)(2 × 2) = 1. Trap: 1/(8√y) mein sirf positive root liya (iska area 1/2 aata hai); √y/2 CDF hai; 1/√y mein density 1/4 se multiply karna bhool gaye (area 4).

questions.question: X ~ Uniform(0, 1) aur Y = −2 ln X. Y ka distribution kya hai? (Yahan Exp(λ) ka matlab rate λ wala Exponential hai.)
questions.explanation: FY(y) = P(−2 ln X ≤ y) = P(X ≥ e^(−y/2)) = 1 − e^(−y/2), y ≥ 0. Yeh Exponential(1/2) hai (rate 1/2, mean 2). Shortcut: −ln X ~ Exp(1), aur cX ~ Exp(λ/c), toh 2 × Exp(1) = Exp(1/2). Trap: Exp(2) mein rate ko 2 se multiply kar diya, jabki time 2 guna hone par rate aadha hota hai; Exp(1) mein factor 2 ignore kiya.

questions.question: X ~ N(10, 4). Constants a > 0 aur b aise chune gaye ki Y = aX + b ~ N(0, 1) ho. b kya hai?
questions.explanation: σ = √4 = 2. Standardization Z = (X − 10)/2 = (1/2)X − 5, toh a = 1/2 aur b = −5. Check: mean (1/2)(10) − 5 = 0, variance (1/2)² × 4 = 1. Trap: −5/2 tab aata hai jab 4 ko σ maan kar a = 1/4 lo (tab variance 1/4 aata hai, 1 nahi); −10 mein μ ko σ se divide nahi kiya.

weeks.title: Multiple continuous RVs
weeks.summary: Do continuous RVs ke liye joint density, marginal density aur independence. Double integral se probabilities aur expectations nikalna seekhenge.
concepts: **Joint PDF**: f(x, y) ≥ 0 aur ∫∫ f(x, y) dx dy = 1. P((X, Y) ∈ A) = region A par f ka double integral.
**Uniform on a region**: f(x, y) = 1/area. Kisi sub-region ki probability = sub-region ka area / total area.
**Marginal PDF**: fX(x) = ∫ f(x, y) dy (y ko integrate out karo). Same tarah fY(y) = ∫ f(x, y) dx.
**Independence**: X, Y independent hain agar f(x, y) = fX(x) × fY(y) har jagah. Support ek rectangle hona chahiye; triangle jaisa support dependence ka sign hai.
**Conditional PDF**: f(y | x) = f(x, y) / fX(x), jahan fX(x) > 0.
**Expectation**: E[g(X, Y)] = ∫∫ g(x, y) f(x, y) dx dy. Linearity yahan bhi chalti hai.
**Sum of independent normals**: X ~ N(μ₁, σ₁²), Y ~ N(μ₂, σ₂²) independent ⇒ X ± Y ~ N(μ₁ ± μ₂, σ₁² + σ₂²).

example.problem: f(x, y) = x + y on 0 ≤ x ≤ 1, 0 ≤ y ≤ 1. Validity check karo, fX(x) nikalo, P(X ≤ 1/2, Y ≤ 1/2) nikalo, aur batao X, Y independent hain ya nahi.
steps: fX(x) = ∫ from 0 to 1 of (x + y) dy = x + 1/2. Isi tarah fY(y) = y + 1/2.
P(X ≤ 1/2, Y ≤ 1/2) = ∫ from 0 to 1/2 [∫ from 0 to 1/2 (x + y) dy] dx = ∫ from 0 to 1/2 (x/2 + 1/8) dx.
fX(x)fY(y) = (x + 1/2)(y + 1/2) ≠ x + y, toh X aur Y independent nahi hain.

mistakes: Uniform region ki density ko hamesha 1 maan lena. Density = 1/area hoti hai.
Triangle region (jaise 0 < y < x < 1) mein integration limits ko 0 se 1 rakh dena. Inner limit doosre variable par depend karti hai.
X − Y ke variance mein variances subtract kar dena. Independent normals ke liye dono variances add hote hain.
revision: X ± Y ~ N(μ₁ ± μ₂, σ₁² + σ₂²) for independent normals

questions.question: (X, Y) ka joint PDF f(x, y) = c hai rectangle 0 ≤ x ≤ 2, 0 ≤ y ≤ 3 par. c kya hai?
questions.explanation: Constant density × area = 1, aur area = 2 × 3 = 6, toh c = 1/6. Trap: 1/5 mein sides add kar di (2 + 3), multiply karna tha.

questions.question: (X, Y) unit square [0, 1] × [0, 1] par uniform hai. P(X + Y ≤ 1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: X + Y ≤ 1 wala region ek triangle hai jiska area 1/2 hai. Total area 1, toh probability 1/2. Trap: 1/4 tab aata hai jab is region ko chhota square samajh lo.

questions.question: f(x, y) = 4xy on [0, 1] × [0, 1]. X ka marginal PDF fX(x) kya hai?
questions.explanation: fX(x) = ∫ from 0 to 1 of 4xy dy = 4x × 1/2 = 2x. Trap: 4x mein y ko integrate karte waqt 1/2 factor bhool gaye; 2xy mein y abhi bhi bacha hai, marginal mein sirf x hona chahiye.

questions.question: f(x, y) = 4xy on [0, 1] × [0, 1]. P(X ≤ 1/2, Y ≤ 1/2) kya hai?
questions.explanation: f = (2x)(2y) hai, toh X, Y independent hain. P(X ≤ 1/2) = ∫ from 0 to 1/2 of 2x dx = 1/4, same Y ke liye. Product = 1/16. Trap: 1/4 region ka area hai, jo sirf uniform density mein probability hota.

questions.question: X ~ N(1, 4) aur Y ~ N(2, 5) independent hain. X − Y ka distribution kya hai?
questions.explanation: Mean = 1 − 2 = −1. Variance = 4 + 5 = 9 (independent RVs ke liye difference mein bhi variances add hote hain). Trap: N(−1, 1) mein variances subtract kiye; N(3, 9) X + Y ka distribution hai.

questions.question: (X, Y) ka joint PDF f(x, y) = 2 hai triangle 0 < y < x < 1 par. E[Y] kya hai?
questions.explanation: fY(y) = ∫ from x = y to 1 of 2 dx = 2(1 − y). E[Y] = ∫ from 0 to 1 of 2y(1 − y) dy = 2(1/2 − 1/3) = 1/3. Trap: 2/3 = E[X] hai (fX(x) = 2x se); 1/2 tab aata hai jab limits 0 se 1 rakh kar triangle ko ignore karo.

questions.question: (X, Y) square [0, 2] × [0, 2] par uniform hai. P(X < 1.5, Y < 0.5) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Density = 1/area = 1/4. Region ka area 1.5 × 0.5 = 0.75, toh probability 0.75/4 = 3/16. Trap: 3/4 mein total area 4 se divide karna bhool gaye (density 1 maan li); 3/8 = (1.5/2) × 0.5 mein Y wale part ko 0.5/2 ki jagah 0.5 liya; 1/4 sirf P(Y < 0.5) hai.

questions.question: (X, Y) ka joint PDF f(x, y) = 8xy hai region 0 < y < x < 1 par (baaki 0). X aur Y ke baare mein kya sahi hai?
options: Dependent hain, kyunki support triangle (y < x) hai, rectangle nahi
Independent hain, kyunki 8xy ko x ke function × y ke function mein tod sakte hain
Independent hain, kyunki region par density hamesha positive hai
Dependent hain, kyunki f(x, y) ki value 1 se zyada ho sakti hai
questions.explanation: Independence ke liye formula factorize hone ke saath support bhi rectangle hona chahiye. Yahan y < x hai: agar X = 0.2 pata ho toh Y 0.2 se chhota hi hoga, yaani Y ki range X par depend karti hai. Trap: sirf 8xy ka factorize hona kaafi nahi; density ka 1 se bada hona dependence ka sign nahi hai.

questions.question: X ~ N(10, 9) aur Y ~ N(4, 16) independent hain. X + Y ka standard deviation kya hai?
questions.explanation: Var(X + Y) = 9 + 16 = 25, toh SD = √25 = 5. Trap: 7 = 3 + 4 mein SDs add kar diye, jabki variances add hote hain, SDs nahi; 25 variance hai, SD nahi; √7 mein variances subtract kar diye.

questions.question: f(x, y) = (3/2)(x² + y²), 0 ≤ x ≤ 1, 0 ≤ y ≤ 1. X ka marginal PDF fX(x) kya hai?
questions.explanation: fX(x) = ∫ from 0 to 1 of (3/2)(x² + y²) dy = (3/2)(x² + 1/3) = (3/2)x² + 1/2. Check: ∫ from 0 to 1 of fX = 1/2 + 1/2 = 1. Trap: (3/2)x² mein y² wala term integrate karna bhool gaye (area sirf 1/2); x² + 1/3 mein constant 3/2 chhoot gaya; 3x² + 1 ka area 2 hai.

questions.question: (X, Y) triangle 0 < y < x < 2 par uniform hai (density 1/2). E[Y | X = 1.2] kya hai?
questions.explanation: fX(x) = ∫ from 0 to x of (1/2) dy = x/2. f(y | x) = (1/2)/(x/2) = 1/x for 0 < y < x, yaani Y | X = x ~ Uniform(0, x). Toh E[Y | X = 1.2] = 1.2/2 = 0.6. Trap: 2/3 = E[Y] hai, bina condition ke; 1 = (0 + 2)/2 mein condition ignore karke Y ki poori range li; 1.2 sirf X ki value hai.

questions.question: X ~ Exp(1) aur Y ~ Exp(2) independent hain (rates 1 aur 2). P(X < Y) kya hai?
questions.explanation: P(X < Y) = ∫ from 0 to ∞ of fX(x) P(Y > x) dx = ∫ from 0 to ∞ of e^(−x) × e^(−2x) dx = 1/3. Intuition: Y ka rate zyada hai, toh Y pehle aane ki probability 2/3 hai aur X pehle aane ki 1/3. Trap: 2/3 = P(Y < X) hai; 1/2 tab aata hai jab dono ko identically distributed maan lo.

questions.question: (X, Y) triangle x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, x + y ≤ 2 par uniform hai. P(X > 1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Total area = (1/2)(2)(2) = 2. X > 1 wala region ek chhota triangle hai, vertices (1,0), (2,0), (1,1), area 1/2. Probability = (1/2)/2 = 1/4. Trap: 1/2 tab aata hai jab X ko Uniform(0, 2) maan lo, jabki X ka marginal (2 − x)/2 hai, uniform nahi; 3/4 = P(X ≤ 1) hai; 1/8 mein total area 4 le liya (poora square).

questions.question: f(x, y) = x + y, 0 ≤ x ≤ 1, 0 ≤ y ≤ 1. Cov(X, Y) kya hai?
questions.explanation: fX(x) = x + 1/2, toh E[X] = ∫ from 0 to 1 of x(x + 1/2) dx = 1/3 + 1/4 = 7/12; symmetry se E[Y] = 7/12. E[XY] = ∫∫ xy(x + y) dx dy = 1/6 + 1/6 = 1/3. Cov = 1/3 − (7/12)² = 48/144 − 49/144 = −1/144. Trap: 1/3 sirf E[XY] hai; 0 tab aata hai jab X, Y ko independent maan lo, jabki f ≠ fX fY; 1/144 mein subtraction ulta kiya.

questions.question: Do runners ke 400 m race times (seconds mein) independent hain: A ~ N(50, 9) aur B ~ N(53, 16). P(A < B) kya hai? (Φ(0.6) ≈ 0.7257, Φ(0.75) ≈ 0.7734, Φ(1) ≈ 0.8413)
questions.explanation: D = A − B ~ N(50 − 53, 9 + 16) = N(−3, 25), SD 5. P(A < B) = P(D < 0) = Φ((0 − (−3))/5) = Φ(0.6) ≈ 0.7257. Trap: 0.2743 = P(D > 0) hai (sign ulta); 0.8413 mein sirf A ka SD 3 use kiya (z = 1); 0.7734 mein sirf B ka SD 4 use kiya (z = 0.75).

weeks.title: Inequalities and limit theorems
weeks.summary: Markov aur Chebyshev inequalities se bina distribution jaane probability ka bound kaise milta hai. Weak law of large numbers aur Central Limit Theorem ka matlab aur use seekhenge.
concepts: **Markov inequality**: X ≥ 0 aur a > 0 ke liye P(X ≥ a) ≤ E[X]/a. Sirf mean chahiye, par bound loose hota hai.
**Chebyshev inequality**: P(|X − μ| ≥ kσ) ≤ 1/k². Equivalent: P(|X − μ| ≥ c) ≤ σ²/c². Kisi bhi distribution ke liye valid.
**Sample mean ke properties**: X̄ = (X₁ + ... + Xₙ)/n ke liye E[X̄] = μ aur Var(X̄) = σ²/n. n badhne par spread kam hota hai.
**Weak Law of Large Numbers (WLLN)**: iid samples ke liye har ε > 0 par P(|X̄ − μ| > ε) → 0 jab n → ∞. Yaani bade sample mein average true mean ke paas aata hai.
**Central Limit Theorem (CLT)**: bade n ke liye X̄ ≈ N(μ, σ²/n) aur sum Sₙ ≈ N(nμ, nσ²), original distribution chahe kuch bhi ho (finite variance ho).
**CLT use karna**: Z = (Sₙ − nμ)/(σ√n) standardize karke Φ table lagao. Binomial ke liye μ = p, σ² = p(1 − p) per trial.

example.problem: 100 iid RVs hain, har ek ka mean 5 aur variance 4. Sum S ke liye P(S > 520) approx nikalo. Saath hi Chebyshev se P(|X̄ − 5| ≥ 0.5) ka upper bound do. (Φ(1) ≈ 0.8413)

mistakes: Chebyshev bound ko exact probability samajh lena. Yeh sirf upper bound hai; asli probability isse kaafi kam ho sakti hai.
X̄ ke standardization mein σ use karna. X̄ ka SD σ/√n hai.
Yeh sochna ki CLT ke baad har individual Xᵢ normal ho jaata hai. Sirf sum ya average approximately normal hota hai.
revision: CLT: X̄ ≈ N(μ, σ²/n), Sₙ ≈ N(nμ, nσ²)

questions.question: X ≥ 0 aur E[X] = 10. Markov inequality se P(X ≥ 50) ka upper bound kya hai?
questions.explanation: Markov: P(X ≥ 50) ≤ 10/50 = 0.2. Trap: 0.8 = 1 − 0.2 hai, jo P(X < 50) ka lower bound hota hai, upper bound nahi.

questions.question: Chebyshev inequality ke hisaab se P(|X − μ| ≥ 3σ) ka upper bound kya hai?
questions.explanation: P(|X − μ| ≥ kσ) ≤ 1/k², k = 3 par 1/9. Trap: 1/3 mein k ko square nahi kiya; 8/9 complement hai, jo andar rehne ka lower bound hai.

questions.question: n = 25 iid observations, har ek ka variance σ² = 16. X̄ ka standard deviation kya hai?
questions.explanation: SD(X̄) = σ/√n = 4/5 = 0.8. Trap: 0.64 = σ²/n hai, yaani variance, SD nahi; 4 ek observation ka SD hai.

questions.question: X ka mean 50 aur variance 25 hai (distribution unknown). Chebyshev se P(40 < X < 60) ka lower bound kya hai?
questions.explanation: σ = 5, toh 10 = 2σ, k = 2. P(|X − 50| ≥ 10) ≤ 1/4, isliye P(40 < X < 60) ≥ 3/4. Trap: 0.95 normal distribution ka 2σ rule hai; yahan distribution unknown hai, toh sirf Chebyshev ka guarantee milta hai.

questions.question: Weak Law of Large Numbers kya kehta hai? (X₁, X₂, ... iid, mean μ)
options: n ≥ 30 hone par X̄ exactly μ ke barabar ho jaata hai
Bade n par har Xᵢ ka distribution normal ho jaata hai
n badhne ke saath Var(X̄) badhta hai
Har ε > 0 ke liye, n → ∞ par P(|X̄ − μ| > ε) → 0
questions.explanation: WLLN kehta hai ki X̄ probability mein μ ki taraf converge karta hai. Trap: X̄ kabhi guaranteed exactly μ nahi hota; normal hone wali baat CLT ki hai aur woh bhi X̄ ke liye, individual Xᵢ ke liye nahi. Var(X̄) = σ²/n ghatta hai.

questions.question: Ek fair coin 100 baar toss hota hai. S = heads ki sankhya. CLT se P(S ≥ 60) approx kya hai? (Continuity correction ignore karo; Φ(1) ≈ 0.8413, Φ(2) ≈ 0.9772, Φ(3) ≈ 0.9987)
X ka mean μ aur variance 4 hai. Chebyshev inequality se P(|X − μ| ≥ 5) ka upper bound kya hai?
questions.explanation: P(|X − μ| ≥ c) ≤ σ²/c² = 4/25 = 0.16. Trap: 0.8 = 4/5 mein c ko square nahi kiya; 0.4 = 2/5 mein σ/c liya, square nahi kiya; 0.84 complement hai, jo andar rehne ka lower bound hai.

questions.question: 64 iid RVs hain, har ek ka mean 2 aur variance 9. CLT se unke sum S ka approx distribution kya hai?
questions.explanation: Sₙ ≈ N(nμ, nσ²) = N(64 × 2, 64 × 9) = N(128, 576). Trap: N(2, 9/64) X̄ ka distribution hai, sum ka nahi; N(128, 72) mein variance ko √64 = 8 se multiply kiya (SD aur variance mix); N(128, 9) mein sum ka variance badhaya hi nahi.

questions.question: X ≥ 0 aur E[X] = 4. Markov inequality P(X < 20) ke baare mein kya guarantee deti hai?
questions.explanation: Markov: P(X ≥ 20) ≤ 4/20 = 0.2. Complement lo: P(X < 20) = 1 − P(X ≥ 20) ≥ 1 − 0.2 = 0.8. Trap: complement lene par inequality ki direction ulat jaati hai, toh '≤ 0.2' galat hai; '= 0.8' galat hai kyunki Markov sirf bound deta hai, exact value nahi.

questions.question: X ≥ 0, E[X] = 6 aur Var(X) = 4. Markov aur Chebyshev dono se P(X ≥ 12) ka upper bound nikalo. Dono mein se behtar (chhota) bound kya hai?
questions.explanation: Markov: P(X ≥ 12) ≤ 6/12 = 1/2. Chebyshev: X ≥ 12 ka matlab X − 6 ≥ 6, toh P(X ≥ 12) ≤ P(|X − 6| ≥ 6) ≤ 4/36 = 1/9. Behtar bound 1/9 hai. Trap: 1/2 Markov wala, kamzor bound hai; 1/3 = 2/6 mein σ/c liya, square nahi kiya; 8/9 complement hai.

questions.question: Ek shop mein har customer ka bill iid hai, mean ₹200 aur SD ₹50 (distribution skewed hai). 100 customers ka average bill ₹210 se zyada hone ki approx probability kya hai? (Φ(0.2) ≈ 0.5793, Φ(2) ≈ 0.9772)
questions.explanation: CLT: X̄ ≈ N(200, 50²/100), SD(X̄) = 50/√100 = 5. z = (210 − 200)/5 = 2. P ≈ 1 − 0.9772 = 0.0228. Distribution skewed hone par bhi n = 100 ke liye CLT kaam karta hai. Trap: 0.4207 = 1 − Φ(0.2) tab aata hai jab X̄ ke liye σ = 50 hi use karo; 0.9772 = P(X̄ ≤ 210) hai; 0.0456 dono tails ka total hai.

questions.question: Ek website par har minute ke visits Poisson(2) hain, alag minutes independent. 50 minutes ke total visits S ke liye CLT se P(S ≤ 90) approx kya hai? (Continuity correction ignore karo; Φ(1) ≈ 0.8413, Φ(0.1) ≈ 0.5398)
questions.explanation: Poisson(2) ka mean = variance = 2. E[S] = 50 × 2 = 100, Var(S) = 50 × 2 = 100, SD = 10. z = (90 − 100)/10 = −1. P(S ≤ 90) ≈ Φ(−1) = 1 − 0.8413 = 0.1587. Trap: 0.4602 = Φ(−0.1) tab aata hai jab variance 100 ko hi SD maan lo; 0.8413 galat tail hai; 0.3174 dono tails ka total hai.

questions.question: Ek fair die 180 baar roll hota hai, S = sixes ki sankhya. CLT se woh value k (approx) kya hai jiske liye P(S ≥ k) ≈ 0.025? (Continuity correction ignore karo; Φ(1.645) ≈ 0.95, Φ(1.96) ≈ 0.975)
questions.explanation: E[S] = 180 × 1/6 = 30, Var(S) = 180 × (1/6)(5/6) = 25, SD = 5. P(S ≥ k) = 0.025 ⇒ (k − 30)/5 = 1.96 ⇒ k = 30 + 9.8 = 39.8. Trap: 38.2 mein 1.645 use kiya (woh 5% tail hai); 40.7 mein variance np = 30 le liya, (1 − p) factor bhool gaye; 79 mein SD ki jagah variance 25 se multiply kiya.

questions.question: X ~ Uniform(0, 12). P(|X − 6| ≥ 4) ka Chebyshev upper bound aur exact value (is order mein) kya hain?
questions.explanation: Mean = 6, Var(X) = 12²/12 = 12. Chebyshev: P(|X − 6| ≥ 4) ≤ 12/16 = 3/4. Exact: X ≤ 2 ya X ≥ 10, total length 4 out of 12, toh 1/3. Bound valid hai par loose. Trap: pehla option order ulta hai; 2/3 = P(|X − 6| < 4) andar wali probability hai; 1/4 = 1 − 3/4 complement hai, bound nahi.

questions.question: Ek election poll mein support ka true proportion p unknown hai. Chebyshev ke hisaab se kam se kam kitne logon ka survey karna chahiye taaki har p ke liye P(|p̂ − p| ≥ 0.1) ≤ 0.05 ho? (Hint: p(1 − p) ≤ 1/4)
questions.explanation: Var(p̂) = p(1 − p)/n ≤ 1/(4n). Chebyshev: P(|p̂ − p| ≥ 0.1) ≤ (1/(4n))/0.1² = 25/n. 25/n ≤ 0.05 ⇒ n ≥ 500. Trap: 50 mein 0.1 ko square nahi kiya; 2000 mein p(1 − p) ki jagah 1 le liya (1/4 wala bound use nahi kiya); 97 CLT wala approx answer hai, Chebyshev ka guarantee nahi.

weeks.title: Samples and statistics
weeks.summary: Population se iid sample lena, aur sample mean, sample variance jaise statistics ke properties. Sample mean ka distribution aur n − 1 se divide karne ki wajah samjhenge.
concepts: **Population vs sample**: population poora group hai jiske parameters (μ, σ²) unknown hain; sample uska chhota hissa hai jisse hum estimate karte hain.
**iid sample**: X₁, ..., Xₙ independent hain aur sab ka distribution population jaisa hai.
**Statistic**: sample ka koi bhi function jisme unknown parameter na ho, jaise X̄, median, max. Statistic khud ek random variable hai.
**Sample mean**: X̄ = ΣXᵢ / n. E[X̄] = μ aur Var(X̄) = σ²/n.
**Sample variance**: S² = Σ(Xᵢ − X̄)² / (n − 1). n − 1 se divide karne par E[S²] = σ², yaani S² unbiased hai.
**Normal population**: agar Xᵢ ~ N(μ, σ²) toh X̄ ~ N(μ, σ²/n) exactly (approx nahi). Doosre populations ke liye bade n par CLT se approx.
**Descriptive statistics**: median (beech wali value), range (max − min), aur sample proportion (successes / n) bhi common statistics hain.

example.problem: Sample: 4, 7, 5, 8, 6. Sample mean, sample variance S² aur median nikalo.

mistakes: Sample variance mein n se divide kar dena. S² ke liye n − 1 use hota hai.
Var(X̄) aur SD(X̄) mix karna. Var(X̄) = σ²/n, SD(X̄) = σ/√n.
Standardize karte waqt X̄ ke liye population ka σ use karna, σ/√n nahi.
revision: X̄ = ΣXᵢ / n; E[X̄] = μ; Var(X̄) = σ²/n

questions.question: Sample 3, 9, 6, 2 ka sample mean kya hai?
questions.explanation: X̄ = (3 + 9 + 6 + 2)/4 = 20/4 = 5. Trap: 20 sirf sum hai, n se divide karna bhool gaye.

questions.question: Sample 2, 4, 6, 8 ka sample variance S² (n − 1 wala) kya hai?
questions.explanation: X̄ = 5. Squared deviations: 9, 1, 1, 9, sum = 20. S² = 20/(4 − 1) = 20/3. Trap: 5 = 20/4 tab aata hai jab n se divide karo; S² mein n − 1 lagta hai.

questions.question: Population variance σ² = 36 hai aur n = 9 ka iid sample liya. Var(X̄) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Var(X̄) = σ²/n = 36/9 = 4. Trap: 2 = σ/√n hai, yaani SD(X̄), variance nahi; 12 = 36/3 mein √n se divide kiya.

questions.question: Sample variance S² mein n ki jagah n − 1 se kyun divide karte hain?
options: Taaki E[S²] = σ² ho, yaani S² unbiased estimator bane
Taaki S² hamesha population variance se chhota aaye
Kyunki sample ka ek data point hamesha outlier hota hai
Taaki S² aur X̄ ki value same aaye
questions.explanation: X̄ khud data se nikla hai, isliye deviations thode chhote aate hain. n − 1 se divide karke yeh correct hota hai aur E[S²] = σ² milta hai. Trap: n − 1 se divide karne par S² bada hota hai, chhota nahi.

questions.question: X₁, ..., X₁₆ iid N(100, 64). P(X̄ > 104) kya hai? (Φ(0.5) ≈ 0.6915, Φ(1) ≈ 0.8413, Φ(2) ≈ 0.9772)
questions.explanation: X̄ ~ N(100, 64/16) = N(100, 4), SD = 2. z = (104 − 100)/2 = 2. P = 1 − 0.9772 = 0.0228. Trap: 0.3085 mein σ = 8 use kiya (√n bhool gaye); 0.1587 mein variance 4 se divide kiya, SD 2 se nahi.

questions.question: iid sample, n = 4, population mean μ = 3 aur variance σ² = 12. E[X̄²] kya hai?
questions.explanation: E[X̄²] = Var(X̄) + (E[X̄])² = 12/4 + 3² = 3 + 9 = 12. Trap: 9 = (E[X̄])² hai, variance part bhool gaye; 21 mein σ² ko n se divide nahi kiya.

questions.question: Sample: 12, 7, 15, 9, 20, 11. Sample median kya hai?
questions.explanation: Pehle sort karo: 7, 9, 11, 12, 15, 20. n = 6 even hai, toh median beech ki do values ka average = (11 + 12)/2 = 11.5. Trap: 12.33 ≈ 74/6 mean hai, median nahi; 13.5 = (7 + 20)/2 min aur max ka average hai; 11 sirf teesri value hai, even n mein beech ki do values ka average lena hota hai.

questions.question: X₁, ..., Xₙ ek iid sample hai jiska population mean μ unknown hai. Inme se kaunsa statistic NAHI hai?
questions.explanation: Statistic sirf sample ka function hota hai, usme koi unknown parameter nahi hona chahiye. X̄ − μ mein unknown μ hai, isliye data se iski value nahi nikal sakte. Trap: max, X₁ + X₂ aur S² sab sirf data se compute hote hain, toh statistics hain (chahe acche estimators hon ya nahi).

questions.question: Population variance σ² = 25 aur n = 10 ka iid sample liya. Sample variance S² (n − 1 wala) ka expected value E[S²] kya hai?
questions.explanation: S² unbiased hai: E[S²] = σ² = 25, n kuch bhi ho. Trap: 2.5 = σ²/n hai, jo Var(X̄) hai; 22.5 = (9/10) × 25 tab aata hai jab n se divide karne wala version lo; 5 = σ hai.

questions.question: Ek sample (n = 10) ke liye Σ(xᵢ − x̄)²/n = 4.5 aaya. Sample variance S² kya hai?
questions.explanation: Σ(xᵢ − x̄)² = 4.5 × 10 = 45. S² = 45/(10 − 1) = 5. Trap: 4.05 = 4.5 × 9/10 mein correction ulta laga diya; 45 sirf sum of squares hai; 4.5 n se divide wala version hai, n − 1 wala nahi.

questions.question: Population SD σ = 12 hai. n = 16 ke sample se SD(X̄) = 3 aata hai. SD(X̄) ko 1 karne ke liye n kitna chahiye?
questions.explanation: SD(X̄) = σ/√n. 12/√n = 1 ⇒ √n = 12 ⇒ n = 144. Yaani SD 3 guna kam karne ke liye n 9 guna (16 × 9 = 144) karna padta hai. Trap: 48 = 16 × 3 tab aata hai jab socho SD 1/n ki tarah ghatta hai; 12 mein σ/n = 1 solve kiya; 256 = 16² hai.

questions.question: iid sample, n = 6, population variance σ² = 10. E[Σ(Xᵢ − X̄)²] kya hai?
questions.explanation: S² = Σ(Xᵢ − X̄)²/(n − 1) aur E[S²] = σ². Toh E[Σ(Xᵢ − X̄)²] = (n − 1)σ² = 5 × 10 = 50. Trap: 60 = nσ² tab sahi hota jab deviations true μ se lete; X̄ data se hi nikalta hai, isliye yeh sum average mein thoda chhota aata hai. 10 = E[S²] hai, sum nahi; 5/3 = σ²/n hai.

questions.question: Ek hi population N(μ, 36) se do independent samples liye: pehla n₁ = 9 ka, doosra n₂ = 4 ka. Var(X̄₁ − X̄₂) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Var(X̄₁) = 36/9 = 4 aur Var(X̄₂) = 36/4 = 9. Samples independent hain, toh difference mein bhi variances add hote hain: 4 + 9 = 13. Trap: 5 = 9 − 4 mein variances subtract kar diye; 36/13 mein dono samples ko ek hi sample (n = 13) maan liya; 72 = 36 + 36 mein n se divide nahi kiya.

questions.question: X₁, X₂, X₃ iid Uniform(0, 1) hain aur statistic M = max(X₁, X₂, X₃). P(M ≤ 0.8) kya hai?
questions.explanation: M ≤ 0.8 tabhi hoga jab teeno ≤ 0.8 hon. Independence se P(M ≤ 0.8) = 0.8³ = 0.512. Trap: 0.8 sirf ek observation ki probability hai; 0.992 = 1 − 0.2³ 'kam se kam ek ≤ 0.8' ki probability hai, yaani min ka event; 0.488 = P(M > 0.8) hai.

weeks.title: Point estimation: MoM and MLE
weeks.summary: Data se unknown parameter ka estimate kaise banayein. Method of moments aur maximum likelihood dono step by step seekhenge, saath mein bias aur MSE.
concepts: **Estimator vs estimate**: estimator ek formula hai (jaise X̄), estimate us formula ki ek number value hai jo data dalne se aati hai.
**Bias aur MSE**: Bias = E[θ̂] − θ. MSE = Var(θ̂) + Bias². Unbiased estimator ka bias 0 hota hai.
**Method of moments (MoM)**: population moments (E[X], E[X²], ...) ko sample moments (X̄, ΣXᵢ²/n, ...) ke barabar rakho aur parameter solve karo.
**Likelihood**: L(θ) = Π f(xᵢ; θ), yaani observed data ki probability (ya density) θ ke function ke roop mein.
**MLE**: L(θ) ko maximize karne wala θ. Practically log-likelihood ln L(θ) lo, derivative 0 rakho, aur solve karo.
**Common MLEs**: Bernoulli p̂ = X̄, Poisson λ̂ = X̄, Exponential λ̂ = 1/X̄, Normal μ̂ = X̄ aur σ̂² = Σ(xᵢ − x̄)²/n.
**Uniform(0, θ) special case**: MLE = max(xᵢ), derivative se nahi milta kyunki L(θ) = 1/θⁿ ghatta function hai jab θ ≥ max. MoM yahan 2X̄ deta hai.

example.problem: Exponential(λ) se sample: 2, 3, 5, 6. λ ka MLE aur MoM estimate nikalo.
steps: L(λ) = Π λe^(−λxᵢ) = λ⁴ e^(−λΣxᵢ), aur Σxᵢ = 16.
MoM: E[X] = 1/λ ko X̄ = 16/4 = 4 ke barabar rakho, toh λ = 1/4 = 0.25.
Answer: dono methods λ̂ = 0.25 dete hain.

mistakes: Uniform(0, θ) ka MLE derivative 0 rakh kar dhoondhna. Yahan answer boundary par hai: θ̂ = max(xᵢ).
MSE mein bias ko square na karna. MSE = Var + Bias².
Log-likelihood mein Σ ln xᵢ ka sign galat le lena. 0 aur 1 ke beech ke x ka ln negative hota hai.
revision: Bias = E[θ̂] − θ; MSE = Var(θ̂) + Bias²
MoM: E[X] = X̄ (aur zarurat ho toh E[X²] = ΣXᵢ²/n)
Bernoulli p̂ = X̄; Poisson λ̂ = X̄; Exponential λ̂ = 1/X̄
Uniform(0, θ): MLE = max xᵢ, MoM = 2X̄

questions.question: Ek coin 20 baar toss kiya, 14 heads aaye. P(Head) = p ka MLE kya hai?
questions.explanation: Bernoulli/Binomial ke liye p̂ = successes / trials = 14/20 = 0.7. Trap: 0.5 fair coin ka assumption hai, data ka estimate nahi; 0.3 tails ka proportion hai.

questions.question: Poisson(λ) se sample: 2, 0, 3, 1, 4. λ ka MLE kya hai?
questions.explanation: Poisson ka MLE λ̂ = X̄ = 10/5 = 2. Trap: 2.5 = 10/4 mein n − 1 se divide kiya; MLE mein simple mean aata hai.

questions.question: Uniform(0, θ) se sample: 1.2, 3.5, 2.8, 0.9. Method of moments se θ ka estimate kya hai?
questions.explanation: E[X] = θ/2. X̄ = 8.4/4 = 2.1. θ/2 = 2.1 ⇒ θ̂ = 4.2. Trap: 2.1 sirf X̄ hai; 3.5 MLE (max) hai, MoM nahi.

questions.question: Uniform(0, θ) se same sample: 1.2, 3.5, 2.8, 0.9. θ ka MLE kya hai?
questions.explanation: L(θ) = 1/θ⁴ jab θ ≥ sab observations, warna 0. Yeh θ badhne par ghatta hai, toh sabse chhota allowed θ = max = 3.5. Trap: 4.2 MoM estimate hai.

questions.question: Ek estimator θ̂ ke liye E[θ̂] = θ + 2 aur Var(θ̂) = 5. MSE kya hai?
questions.explanation: Bias = 2. MSE = Var + Bias² = 5 + 4 = 9. Trap: 7 mein bias ko square nahi kiya; 5 sirf variance hai.

questions.question: PDF f(x; θ) = θx^(θ − 1), 0 < x < 1, θ > 0. n = 4 observations ke liye Σ ln xᵢ = −8. θ ka MLE kya hai?
questions.explanation: ln L = n ln θ + (θ − 1)Σ ln xᵢ. Derivative: n/θ + Σ ln xᵢ = 0 ⇒ θ̂ = −n / Σ ln xᵢ = −4/(−8) = 0.5. Trap: 2 = 8/4 ulta fraction hai; −0.5 mein minus sign bhool gaye (θ > 0 hona chahiye).

questions.question: Exponential(λ) se sample: 1.5, 2.5, 4, 2. λ ka MLE kya hai?
questions.explanation: Exponential ke liye λ̂ = 1/X̄. X̄ = 10/4 = 2.5, toh λ̂ = 1/2.5 = 0.4. Trap: 2.5 sirf X̄ hai (mean ka estimate, rate ka nahi); 0.1 = 1/Σxᵢ mein n bhool gaye; 0.3 = 3/10 mein n ki jagah n − 1 le liya.

questions.question: Ek estimator θ̂ ke liye E[θ̂] = 0.9θ. Iska bias kya hai?
questions.explanation: Bias = E[θ̂] − θ = 0.9θ − θ = −0.1θ. Negative bias ka matlab estimator average mein θ ko underestimate karta hai. Trap: 0.1θ mein subtraction ulta kiya (θ − E[θ̂]); 0.9θ sirf E[θ̂] hai; 1.9θ mein θ add kar diya.

questions.question: Normal(μ, σ²) se sample: 2, 4, 6. σ² ka MLE kya hai?
questions.explanation: x̄ = 4. Σ(xᵢ − x̄)² = 4 + 0 + 4 = 8. Normal ka MLE σ̂² = Σ(xᵢ − x̄)²/n = 8/3. Trap: 4 = 8/(3 − 1) sample variance S² hai, jabki MLE n se divide karta hai; 8 sirf sum of squares hai; √(8/3) σ ka estimate hai, σ² ka nahi.

questions.question: θ ke do estimators hain: θ̂₁ unbiased hai aur Var(θ̂₁) = 6; θ̂₂ ka bias 2 hai aur Var(θ̂₂) = 4. MSE ke hisaab se kaunsa behtar hai?
options: Dono barabar, kyunki dono ka MSE 6 hai
questions.explanation: MSE = Var + Bias². θ̂₁: 6 + 0² = 6. θ̂₂: 4 + 2² = 8. Chhota MSE behtar hai, toh θ̂₁. Trap: 'dono 6' tab aata hai jab bias ko square na karo (4 + 2); sirf variance compare karna bias ko ignore karta hai; 'MSE 4' mein bias bilkul chhod diya.

questions.question: Normal(μ, σ²) se n = 5 observations: Σxᵢ = 20 aur Σxᵢ² = 120. Method of moments se σ² ka estimate kya hai?
questions.explanation: Pehla moment: X̄ = 20/5 = 4 = μ̂. Doosra moment: E[X²] = σ² + μ² ko Σxᵢ²/n = 120/5 = 24 ke barabar rakho. σ̂² = 24 − 4² = 8. Trap: 24 mein μ² ghatana bhool gaye; 10 = (120 − 80)/4 sample variance S² (n − 1 wala) hai, MoM nahi; 104 = 120 − 16 mein Σxᵢ² ko n se divide nahi kiya.

questions.question: Uniform(−θ, θ) se sample: 0, 3, −3, 1, −1. Method of moments se θ ka estimate kya hai? (Uniform(a, b) ka variance (b − a)²/12 hai)
questions.explanation: E[X] = 0 har θ ke liye, toh pehle moment se θ nahi milta. Second moment: E[X²] = Var + 0² = (2θ)²/12 = θ²/3. Sample se Σxᵢ²/n = (0 + 9 + 9 + 1 + 1)/5 = 4. θ²/3 = 4 ⇒ θ = √12 = 2√3 ≈ 3.46. Trap: 3 = max|xᵢ| hai, jo MLE hai, MoM nahi; 2 = √4 mein factor 3 bhool gaye; 0 pehle moment se aata hai, jo θ ke baare mein kuch nahi batata.

questions.question: PDF f(x; θ) = 2x/θ², 0 < x < θ. Sample: 1.2, 0.7, 2.6, 1.9. θ ka MLE kya hai?
questions.explanation: L(θ) = Π(2xᵢ)/θ⁸ jab θ ≥ sab xᵢ, warna 0. Yeh θ badhne par ghatta hai, toh sabse chhota allowed θ = max xᵢ = 2.6. Derivative 0 rakhne se answer nahi milta. Trap: 2.4 MoM estimate hai (E[X] = 2θ/3 aur X̄ = 1.6, toh θ = 1.5 × 1.6); 3.2 = 2X̄ Uniform wala MoM formula galat jagah laga diya; 1.6 sirf X̄ hai.

questions.question: PDF f(x; θ) = θ²x e^(−θx), x > 0. n = 5 observations ka Σxᵢ = 4 hai. θ ka MLE kya hai?
questions.explanation: ln L = 2n ln θ + Σ ln xᵢ − θΣxᵢ. Derivative: 2n/θ − Σxᵢ = 0 ⇒ θ̂ = 2n/Σxᵢ = 10/4 = 2.5. Trap: 1.25 = n/Σxᵢ tab aata hai jab θ² ki power 2 bhool kar Exponential jaisa 1/X̄ le lo; 0.8 = X̄ hai; 1.6 = 2X̄ ulta fraction hai.

questions.question: X₁, X₂, X₃ iid hain, mean μ = 4 aur variance σ² = 4. Estimator μ̂ = (X₁ + X₂ + X₃)/4 hai. Is estimator ka MSE kya hai?
questions.explanation: E[μ̂] = 3μ/4 = 3, toh Bias = 3 − 4 = −1. Var(μ̂) = 3σ²/16 = 12/16 = 0.75. MSE = Var + Bias² = 0.75 + (−1)² = 1.75. Trap: 0.75 sirf variance hai; 1 sirf Bias² hai; 7/3 = 4/3 + 1 mein variance 3σ²/9 le liya, jaise 3 se divide ho raha ho.

weeks.title: Bayesian estimation
weeks.summary: Parameter ko random variable maan kar prior belief ko data se update karna. Bayes theorem se posterior, aur Beta prior ke saath coin-toss problems seekhenge.
concepts: **Bayesian idea**: unknown parameter θ ko random maana jaata hai. Data dekhne se pehle ka belief **prior** hai, data ke baad ka updated belief **posterior**.
**Bayes rule for parameters**: posterior ∝ likelihood × prior. Discrete prior mein har θ value ke liye likelihood × prior nikalo, phir total se divide karo.
**Beta prior**: p (0 aur 1 ke beech) ke liye Beta(α, β) prior common hai. Prior mean = α/(α + β). Beta(1, 1) = Uniform(0, 1).
**Conjugate update**: Beta(α, β) prior + n tosses mein k heads ⇒ posterior Beta(α + k, β + n − k). Heads α mein, tails β mein jud jaate hain.
**Posterior mean**: Beta posterior ka mean (α + k)/(α + β + n). Yeh prior mean aur MLE k/n ke beech aata hai.
**Bade data ka asar**: n bahut bada ho toh posterior mean MLE ke kareeb aa jaata hai, prior ka asar kam ho jaata hai.

example.problem: Ek coin ka p ya toh 0.5 hai ya 0.8, dono ki prior probability 1/2. Do toss mein dono Heads aaye. P(p = 0.8 | data) nikalo.
steps: Likelihood: p = 0.5 par P(HH) = 0.25; p = 0.8 par P(HH) = 0.64.
Answer: ≈ 0.719. Do heads dekhne ke baad belief 0.5 se badhkar lagbhag 0.72 ho gaya.

mistakes: Posterior nikalte waqt total (normalising constant) se divide karna bhool jaana.
Beta update mein tails ko β mein na jodna. Posterior Beta(α + heads, β + tails) hota hai.
Prior probability ko hi answer maan lena, jaise P(bad machine) = 0.2, jabki data ke baad belief update hona chahiye.
revision: Beta(α, β) + k heads in n ⇒ Beta(α + k, β + n − k)

questions.question: p par prior Beta(2, 3) hai. Prior mean kya hai?
questions.explanation: Beta(α, β) ka mean α/(α + β) = 2/5. Trap: 2/3 = α/β hai, aur 3/5 = β/(α + β) jo ulta hai.

questions.question: Coin ke p par Beta(1, 1) prior lene ka matlab kya hai?
options: p = 0.5 par poora belief concentrated hai
Uniform(0, 1) prior, yaani 0 aur 1 ke beech har value equally plausible
questions.explanation: Beta(1, 1) ki density 0 se 1 tak constant 1 hai, yaani Uniform(0, 1). Yeh 'koi khaas preference nahi' wala prior hai. Trap: iska mean 0.5 hai, par belief 0.5 par concentrated nahi, poori range mein faila hua hai.

questions.question: p par prior Beta(2, 2) hai. 10 tosses mein 7 heads aaye. Posterior distribution kya hai?
questions.explanation: Posterior = Beta(α + heads, β + tails) = Beta(2 + 7, 2 + 3) = Beta(9, 5). Trap: Beta(9, 12) mein β mein total tosses jod diye; Beta(5, 9) ulta hai; Beta(7, 3) prior ignore karta hai.

questions.question: Posterior Beta(9, 5) hai. Posterior mean kya hai?
questions.explanation: Mean = α/(α + β) = 9/14 ≈ 0.643. Yeh prior mean 0.5 aur MLE 0.7 ke beech hai. Trap: 7/10 MLE hai (sirf data); 9/5 = α/β hai, jo probability bhi nahi ho sakta (1 se bada).

questions.question: Machine 'good' hai (defect rate 0.1) probability 0.8 se, ya 'bad' hai (defect rate 0.5) probability 0.2 se. Ek item test kiya, defective nikla. P(bad | defective)?
questions.explanation: Bad: 0.2 × 0.5 = 0.1. Good: 0.8 × 0.1 = 0.08. Total = 0.18. Posterior = 0.1/0.18 = 5/9 ≈ 0.556. Trap: 0.1 numerator hai, total se divide nahi kiya; 0.2 prior hai, data ka update nahi hua.

questions.question: p par prior Beta(3, 3) hai. 4 tosses mein 4 heads aaye. Posterior mean aur MLE kya hain (is order mein)?
questions.explanation: Posterior = Beta(3 + 4, 3 + 0) = Beta(7, 3), mean = 7/10 = 0.7. MLE = 4/4 = 1. Prior ne estimate ko extreme value 1 se pull back kiya. Trap: 0.75 = (α − 1)/(α + β − 2) = 6/8 posterior ka mode hai, mean nahi.

questions.question: Bayesian estimation mein parameter θ ka posterior kis cheez ke proportional hota hai?
questions.explanation: Bayes rule: posterior ∝ likelihood × prior. Phir sab θ values ke total se divide karke normalise karte hain. Trap: 'sirf prior' data ko ignore karta hai; likelihood aur prior ko add ya divide karne se Bayes rule nahi banta.

questions.question: p par Beta(α, β) prior hai jiska mean 0.25 hai aur α + β = 8. α kya hai?
questions.explanation: Prior mean α/(α + β) = α/8 = 0.25 ⇒ α = 2 (aur β = 6). Trap: 6 = β hai, ulta le liya; 1/4 mean hai, α nahi; 4 = 8/2 equal split maan leta hai.

questions.question: Ek coin ka p ya toh 0.2 hai ya 0.6, dono ki prior probability 1/2. Ek toss mein Head aaya. P(p = 0.6 | Head) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Likelihood × prior: p = 0.2 ke liye 0.2 × 0.5 = 0.1, p = 0.6 ke liye 0.6 × 0.5 = 0.3. Total = 0.4. Posterior = 0.3/0.4 = 0.75. Trap: 0.6 likelihood P(Head | p = 0.6) hai, posterior nahi; 0.5 prior hai; 0.3 mein total se divide (normalise) karna bhool gaye.

questions.question: p par Uniform(0, 1), yaani Beta(1, 1), prior hai. 10 tosses mein 3 heads aaye. Posterior mean kya hai?
questions.explanation: Posterior = Beta(1 + 3, 1 + 7) = Beta(4, 8). Mean = 4/(4 + 8) = 1/3. Trap: 0.3 = 3/10 MLE hai, prior ignore kiya; 1/2 = 4/8 = α/β hai; 1/4 = 3/12 mein heads mein prior ka 1 nahi joda.

questions.question: p par prior Beta(2, 2) hai. Pehle din 3 tosses mein 2 heads aaye, doosre din 5 tosses mein 1 head aaya. Dono din ke baad posterior kya hai?
questions.explanation: Total heads = 2 + 1 = 3, total tails = 1 + 4 = 5. Posterior = Beta(2 + 3, 2 + 5) = Beta(5, 7). (Din 1 ka posterior Beta(4, 3) din 2 ka prior banta hai; usse bhi Beta(4 + 1, 3 + 4) = Beta(5, 7).) Trap: Beta(3, 6) mein sirf doosre din ka data joda; Beta(5, 10) mein β mein total tosses 8 jod diye; Beta(7, 5) mein heads aur tails ulte hain.

questions.question: Ek coin ka p teen values mein se ek hai: 0.2, 0.5, 0.8, prior probabilities 0.3, 0.4, 0.3. 2 tosses mein pehle Head phir Tail aaya. P(p = 0.5 | data) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Likelihood p(1 − p): 0.16, 0.25, 0.16. × prior: 0.048, 0.1, 0.048. Total = 0.196. Posterior = 0.1/0.196 = 25/49 ≈ 0.510. Trap: 0.4 prior hai; 0.1 normalise nahi kiya; 0.25 sirf likelihood hai.

questions.question: p par Beta(α, β) prior hai jahan α + β = 10. 30 tosses mein 18 heads aaye aur posterior mean exactly 0.5 aaya. α kya hai?
questions.explanation: Posterior mean = (α + 18)/(α + β + 30) = (α + 18)/40 = 0.5 ⇒ α + 18 = 20 ⇒ α = 2 (β = 8). Trap: 5 tab aata hai jab prior mean ko 0.5 maan lo, jabki posterior mean prior mean nahi hai; 8 mein heads ki jagah tails (12) joda; 20 = α + 18 posterior ka pehla parameter hai, prior ka α nahi.

questions.question: Ek box mein 3 coins hain: 2 fair aur 1 double-headed (dono taraf Head). Ek random coin chuna aur 2 baar toss kiya; dono baar Head aaya. P(double-headed | HH) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Prior: double-headed 1/3, fair 2/3. HH ki likelihood: double-headed ke liye 1, fair ke liye 1/4. Likelihood × prior: 1/3 aur (2/3)(1/4) = 1/6. Posterior = (1/3)/(1/3 + 1/6) = 2/3. Trap: 1/3 prior hai; 4/5 = 1/(1 + 1/4) tab aata hai jab prior equal (1/2, 1/2) maan lo, jabki fair coins 2 hain; 1/2 sirf ek rough guess hai.

questions.question: p par prior Beta(4, 6) hai. 100 tosses mein 70 heads aaye. Posterior mean kya hai?
questions.explanation: Posterior = Beta(4 + 70, 6 + 30) = Beta(74, 36), mean = 74/110 ≈ 0.673. Yeh prior mean 0.4 aur MLE 0.7 ke beech hai, aur n bada hone ki wajah se MLE ke kaafi kareeb hai. Trap: 0.7 MLE hai; 0.4 prior mean hai; 0.55 dono ka simple average hai, jabki weight data ke size par depend karta hai.

weeks.title: Hypothesis testing basics
weeks.summary: Data se kisi claim ko test karna: null aur alternative hypothesis, Type I/II errors, z-test aur p-value. Decision rule step by step lagana seekhenge.
concepts: **H0 aur H1**: null hypothesis H0 default claim hai (jaise μ = 50); alternative H1 woh hai jo hum evidence se dikhana chahte hain (jaise μ < 50).
**Test statistic aur rejection region**: data se ek number (jaise Z) nikalo; agar woh rejection region mein gire toh H0 reject karo.
**Type I error**: H0 true hai phir bhi reject kar diya. Iski probability α = significance level.
**Type II error aur power**: H0 false hai par reject nahi kiya, probability β. **Power** = 1 − β = H0 false hone par sahi se reject karne ki probability.
**z-test for mean (σ known)**: Z = (X̄ − μ₀)/(σ/√n). α = 0.05 par one-tailed critical value 1.645, two-tailed 1.96.
**p-value**: H0 true maan kar, itna ya isse zyada extreme result aane ki probability. Rule: p-value ≤ α ⇒ reject H0.
**Fail to reject ≠ accept**: H0 reject na hona ka matlab H0 prove ho gaya nahi; bas evidence kaafi nahi tha.

example.problem: Company kehti hai battery ka mean life 50 hours hai (σ = 6). 36 batteries ka x̄ = 48 aaya. α = 0.05 par test karo H0: μ = 50 vs H1: μ < 50. (Φ(2) ≈ 0.9772)
steps: Left-tailed test, α = 0.05: critical value −1.645. Reject agar Z < −1.645.
Answer: H0 reject; data suggest karta hai ki mean life 50 hours se kam hai.

mistakes: Z mein σ/√n ki jagah sirf σ use karna. Sample mean ka spread σ/√n hota hai.
Two-tailed test mein 1.645 use karna. Two-tailed α = 0.05 ke liye 1.96 lagta hai.
Fail to reject ko 'H0 true prove ho gaya' bol dena.
revision: α = P(reject H0 | H0 true) = Type I error
β = P(not reject H0 | H1 true); power = 1 − β

questions.question: Type I error kya hai?
options: H0 true hone par bhi H0 ko reject karna
H0 false hone par H0 ko reject na karna
H1 true hone par H1 ko accept karna
questions.explanation: Type I error = true H0 ko galti se reject karna, probability α. Trap: 'H0 false hone par reject na karna' Type II error hai.

questions.question: Kisi test ki power kya hoti hai? (α = Type I error probability, β = Type II error probability)
questions.explanation: Power = H0 false hone par use reject karne ki probability = 1 − β. Trap: 1 − α true H0 ko sahi se accept karne ki probability hai, power nahi.

questions.question: σ = 10, n = 25, H0: μ = 60. Sample mean x̄ = 63. Test statistic Z kya hai?
questions.explanation: Z = (63 − 60)/(10/√25) = 3/2 = 1.5. Trap: 0.3 = 3/10 mein √n bhool gaye; 3 sirf difference hai, standardize nahi kiya.

questions.question: Two-tailed z-test, α = 0.05, aur Z = 1.5 aaya. Sahi decision kya hai?
options: Reject H0, kyunki Z positive hai
questions.explanation: Two-tailed α = 0.05 par critical value 1.96. |1.5| < 1.96, toh rejection region mein nahi, fail to reject. Trap: fail to reject ka matlab H0 prove hona nahi; aur Z ko seedha α se compare nahi karte, p-value ko karte hain.

questions.question: Ek test ka p-value 0.03 aaya. α = 0.05 aur α = 0.01 par decision kya hoga?
options: α = 0.05 par reject, α = 0.01 par fail to reject
α = 0.01 par reject, α = 0.05 par fail to reject
Dono levels par fail to reject
questions.explanation: Rule: p-value ≤ α ⇒ reject. 0.03 ≤ 0.05 toh reject; 0.03 > 0.01 toh fail to reject. Trap: chhota α zyada strict hota hai, reject karna mushkil hota hai, aasaan nahi.

questions.question: Normal population, σ = 8, n = 16. H0: μ = 10 ko reject karte hain agar X̄ > 12. Type I error α aur μ = 14 par power kya hain (is order mein)? (Φ(0.5) ≈ 0.6915, Φ(1) ≈ 0.8413)
questions.explanation: SD(X̄) = 8/√16 = 2. α = P(X̄ > 12 | μ = 10) = P(Z > 1) = 0.1587. Power = P(X̄ > 12 | μ = 14) = P(Z > −1) = 0.8413. Trap: 0.3085/0.6915 tab aata hai jab variance 4 ko SD le lo (z = 0.5); pehla option order ulta hai.

questions.question: Ek nayi delivery app claim karti hai ki uska average delivery time 30 minutes se kam hai. Is claim ko data se support karne ke liye sahi H0 aur H1 kya hain?
questions.explanation: Jo claim evidence se dikhana hai woh H1 mein jaata hai: μ < 30. H0 default wala claim μ = 30 hai. Trap: H0 mein '<' rakhna ulta hai; '>' galat direction hai; '≠' two-sided hai, jabki claim ek hi direction ka hai.

questions.question: Right-tailed z-test, α = 0.05. H0 kab reject karenge?
questions.explanation: One-tailed α = 0.05 ka critical value 1.645 hai, kyunki Φ(1.645) ≈ 0.95. Trap: 1.96 two-tailed test ka value hai (har tail mein 0.025); 2.33 α = 0.01 ka one-tailed value hai; Z ko seedha α se compare nahi karte.

questions.question: Right-tailed z-test mein Z = 1.8 aaya. p-value kya hai? (Φ(1.8) ≈ 0.9641)
questions.explanation: Right-tailed p-value = P(Z ≥ 1.8) = 1 − 0.9641 = 0.0359. Trap: 0.9641 = P(Z < 1.8) hai, ulta tail; 0.0718 two-tailed p-value hota; 0.4641 = Φ(1.8) − 0.5 hai.

questions.question: Two-tailed z-test mein Z = −2.2 aaya. p-value kya hai? (Φ(2.2) ≈ 0.9861)
questions.explanation: Two-tailed p-value = 2 × P(Z ≤ −2.2) = 2 × (1 − 0.9861) = 2 × 0.0139 = 0.0278. Trap: 0.0139 sirf ek tail hai, two-tailed mein dono tails count hoti hain; 0.9861 aur 0.9722 galat side ka area hain.

questions.question: H0: μ = 200 vs H1: μ > 200, σ = 30, n = 36, x̄ = 207, α = 0.05. Test statistic aur decision kya hai?
questions.explanation: σ/√n = 30/6 = 5. Z = (207 − 200)/5 = 1.4. Right-tailed critical value 1.645 hai, aur 1.4 < 1.645, toh fail to reject H0. Trap: 'reject' galat hai kyunki 1.4 rejection region mein nahi aata; 0.23 = 7/30 mein √n bhool gaye; 8.4 = 7/(30/36) mein n se divide kiya, √n se nahi.

questions.question: Normal population, σ = 12, n = 36. H0: μ = 100 ko reject karte hain agar X̄ < 97. Agar asal mean μ = 95 ho, toh Type II error ki probability β kya hai? (Φ(1) ≈ 0.8413, Φ(1.5) ≈ 0.9332)
questions.explanation: SD(X̄) = 12/√36 = 2. Type II error = H0 false (μ = 95) hone par bhi reject na karna = P(X̄ ≥ 97 | μ = 95) = P(Z ≥ (97 − 95)/2) = P(Z ≥ 1) = 1 − 0.8413 = 0.1587. Trap: 0.8413 power hai (sahi reject karna); 0.0668 = P(X̄ < 97 | μ = 100) = α hai, yaani Type I error; 0.9332 = 1 − α hai.

questions.question: H0: μ = 80 vs H1: μ ≠ 80, σ = 15, n = 25, α = 0.05. Inme se kis sample mean par H0 reject hoga?
questions.explanation: σ/√n = 15/5 = 3. Two-tailed α = 0.05: reject agar |Z| > 1.96, yaani x̄ < 80 − 5.88 = 74.12 ya x̄ > 85.88. x̄ = 86.1 par Z = 6.1/3 ≈ 2.03 > 1.96, toh reject. Trap: 85.5 aur 74.5 par |Z| ≈ 1.83, jo 1.645 se bada par 1.96 se chhota hai; one-tailed cutoff lagaoge toh galti se reject kar doge. 77 par Z = −1.

questions.question: Ek researcher 20 alag aur independent tests karta hai, har ek α = 0.05 par, aur sabhi mein H0 asal mein true hai. Kam se kam ek test mein galti se H0 reject hone (Type I error) ki probability kya hai?
questions.explanation: Har test mein galat rejection na hone ki probability 0.95 hai. Tests independent hain, toh saare 20 mein koi galat rejection na ho = 0.95^20 ≈ 0.358. Kam se kam ek = 1 − 0.358 ≈ 0.642. Trap: 20 × 0.05 = 1 mein probabilities add kar di (overlap double count hota hai, aur probability 1 nahi ho sakti); 0.05 sirf ek test ka α hai; 0.358 'ek bhi error nahi' wali probability hai.

questions.question: Normal population, σ = 4, n = 16. H0: μ = 20 vs H1: μ > 20 ka test aise banaya gaya ki α = 0.0228 ho. μ = 23 par test ki power kya hai? (Φ(1) ≈ 0.8413, Φ(2) ≈ 0.9772)
questions.explanation: SD(X̄) = 4/√16 = 1. α = 0.0228 ⇒ critical z = 2 (kyunki Φ(2) = 0.9772), toh reject jab X̄ > 20 + 2 × 1 = 22. Power = P(X̄ > 22 | μ = 23) = P(Z > −1) = 0.8413. Trap: 0.1587 = β (Type II error) hai; 0.0228 = α hai, power nahi; 0.5 tab aata hai jab cutoff ko galti se 23 maan lo.
